title.zh: 卷八十三 列傳第二十一: 張通古 張浩子:汝霖 張玄素 張汝弼 耶律安禮 納合椿年 祁宰
title.en: Volume 83 Biographies 21: Zhang Tonggu, Zhang Hao Son: Rulin, Zhang Xuansu, Zhang Rubi, Ye Luanli, Na Hechunnian, Qi Zai
title.raw: 卷八十三 列傳第二十一: 張通古 張浩子:汝霖 張玄素 張汝弼 耶律安禮 納合椿年 祁宰 Volume 83 Biographies 21: Zhang Tonggu, Zhang Hao Son: Rulin, Zhang Xuansu, Zhang Rubi, Ye Luanli, Na Hechunnian, Qi Zai

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十一 ○張通古 張浩子:汝霖 張玄素 張汝弼 耶律安禮 納合椿年 祁宰

translations.literal: Biographies 21 ○ Zhang Tonggu, Zhang Hao son: Rulin, Zhang Xuansu, Zhang Rubi, Yelu Anli, Na Hechunnian, Qi Zai
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 21: Zhang Tonggu; Zhang Hao, son Rulin; Zhang Xuansu; Zhang Rubi; Yelu Anli; Na Hechunnian; and Qi Zai

sentences.zh: 張通古

translations.literal: Zhang Tonggu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tonggu

sentences.zh: 張通古，字樂之，易州易縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang Tonggu, style name Lezhi, was a native of Yi County in Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tonggu, whose style name was Lezhi, came from Yi County in Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 讀書過目不忘，該綜經史，善屬文。

translations.literal: In reading, whatever passed his eyes he did not forget; he mastered the classics and histories comprehensively, and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he read stayed with him at a glance; he commanded the full range of classical learning and history, and wrote with uncommon skill.

sentences.zh: 遼天慶二年進士第，補樞密院令史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqing of Liao he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed a clerk of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the second year of the Liao era name Tianqing (1112) and took a post as clerk in the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起複，懇辭不獲，因遁去，屏居興平。

translations.literal: When in mourning for his father, he was recalled from mourning to serve; he earnestly declined but could not refuse, and so fled away and lived in seclusion at Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death, the court recalled him from mourning back to office; he pleaded to stay home but was overruled, so he slipped away and withdrew to live quietly at Xingping.

sentences.zh: 太祖定燕京，割以與宋。

translations.literal: When Taizu pacified Yanjing, he ceded it to Song.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin founder Taizu took Yanjing, the city was handed over to the Song.

sentences.zh: 宋人欲收人望，召通古。

translations.literal: The Song wished to win men of reputation and summoned Tonggu.
translations.idiomatic: The Song court, eager to attract distinguished talent, summoned Tonggu.

sentences.zh: 通古辭謝，隱居易州太寧山下。

translations.literal: Tonggu declined and took refuge below Mount Taining in Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tonggu refused the offer and went into hiding at the foot of Mount Taining in Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宗望複燕京，侍中劉彥宗與通古素善，知其才，召為樞密院主奏，改兵刑房承旨。

translations.literal: When Zongwang recovered Yanjing, the Palace Attendant Liu Yanzong had long been on good terms with Tonggu and knew his talent; he summoned him as chief memorialist of the Privy Council, and changed his post to Bureau Director of the Military and Punishments section.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzongwang reclaimed Yanjing, Liu Yanzong—already a friend—recognized Tonggu's ability and made him chief memorialist in the Privy Council, then transferred him to head the military and punishments bureau.

sentences.zh: 天會四年，初建尚書省，除工部侍郎，兼六部事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianhui, when the Department of State Affairs was first established, he was appointed Vice Minister of Works and concurrently handled the affairs of all six ministries.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianhui (1126), with the new Department of State Affairs in place, he was made Vice Minister of Works and put in charge of all six ministries at once.

sentences.zh: 高慶裔設磨勘法，仕宦者多奪官，通古亦免去。

translations.literal: Gao Qingyi established the merit-review law, and many officials had their posts stripped; Tonggu was also removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qingyi introduced a merit-review system that stripped many officials of their posts, and Tonggu lost his office as well.

sentences.zh: 遼王宗幹素知通古名，惜其才，遣人諭之使自理。

translations.literal: Prince Zonggan of Liao had long known Tonggu's reputation, valued his talent, and sent someone to instruct him to plead his own case.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zonggan had long known Tonggu by reputation and valued his talent; he sent an envoy urging him to plead his own case and win reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 通古不肯，曰：「多士皆去，而己何心，獨求用哉！」

translations.literal: Tonggu would not agree, saying, "Many scholars have all left office—what heart would I have to seek employment alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Tonggu refused, saying, "So many men of learning have already left office—what sort of heart would I have to seek a post for myself alone?"

sentences.zh: 宗幹為論理之。

translations.literal: Zonggan argued the reasoning on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Zonggan argued the case on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 除中京副留守，為詔諭江南使，宋主欲南面，使通古北面。

translations.literal: He was appointed Deputy Military Commissioner of the Central Capital and made envoy to proclaim the edict in Jiangnan; the Song ruler wished to face south while making Tonggu face north.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Deputy Military Commissioner of the Central Capital and sent as envoy to deliver the imperial edict to the south; the Song emperor wanted to face south while obliging Tonggu to face north.

sentences.zh: 通古曰：「大國之卿當小國之君。

translations.literal: Tonggu said, "A minister of a great state stands before the ruler of a small state.
translations.idiomatic: Tonggu said, "A minister of a great power should stand before the ruler of a lesser state.

sentences.zh: 天子以河南、陝西賜之宋，宋約奉表稱臣，使者不可以北面。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven granted Henan and Shaanxi to Song, and Song agreed to submit memorials as a subject; an envoy may not face north.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has granted Henan and Shaanxi to Song, and Song has pledged to submit memorials as a vassal—an envoy cannot be made to face north.

sentences.zh: 若欲貶損使者，使者不敢傳詔。」

translations.literal: If you wish to demean the envoy, the envoy dare not transmit the edict."
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to demean the envoy, the envoy will not dare deliver the edict."

sentences.zh: 遂索馬欲北歸。

translations.literal: He then demanded horses and prepared to return north.
translations.idiomatic: He then called for his horses and prepared to return north.

sentences.zh: 宋主遽命設東西位，使者東面，宋主西面，受詔拜起皆如儀。

translations.literal: The Song ruler hastily ordered east and west seats set up: the envoy faced east, the Song ruler faced west, and receiving the edict, bowing, and rising all followed proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor hastily had east and west seats arranged—the envoy facing east, the emperor facing west—and the reception of the edict, bowing, and rising all followed proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 使還，聞宋已置戍河南，謂送伴韓肖胄曰：「天子裂壤地益南國，南國當思圖報大恩。

translations.literal: On his return from the mission, hearing that Song had already posted garrisons in Henan, he said to the escort Han Xiaozhou, "The Son of Heaven has carved out territory to enlarge the Southern State; the Southern State ought to think how to repay this great grace.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he learned that Song had already posted garrisons in Henan, and said to his escort Han Xiaozhou, "The Son of Heaven has carved out territory to enlarge your southern realm; the south ought to think how to repay so great a favor.

sentences.zh: 今輒置守戍，自取嫌疑，若興師問罪，將何以為辭？

translations.literal: Now you rashly set up guards and garrisons, inviting suspicion on yourselves; if troops are raised to demand an accounting, what excuse will you have?
translations.idiomatic: Now you rashly post guards and invite suspicion; if an army marches to demand an accounting, what excuse will you offer?

sentences.zh: 江左且不可保，況齊乎？」

translations.literal: The lands south of the Yangzi cannot even be secured—how much less Qi?"
translations.idiomatic: The lands south of the Yangzi cannot even be held secure—how much less the Qi region?"

sentences.zh: 肖胄惶恐曰：「敬聞命矣。」

translations.literal: Xiaozhou said in alarm, "I have respectfully heard your command."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhou said in alarm, "I have heard and will obey."

sentences.zh: 即馳白宋主。

translations.literal: He immediately galloped off to report to the Song ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately galloped off to report to the Song emperor.

sentences.zh: 宋主遽命罷戍。

translations.literal: The Song ruler hastily ordered the garrisons withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor hastily ordered the garrisons withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 通古至上京，具以白宗幹，且曰：「及其部置未定，當議收復。」

translations.literal: Tonggu reached the Supreme Capital and reported everything fully to Zonggan, adding, "While their dispositions are not yet settled, we ought to discuss recovering the territory."
translations.idiomatic: Tonggu reached the Supreme Capital and reported everything to Zonggan, adding, "While their deployments are still unsettled, we ought to discuss taking the territory back."

sentences.zh: 宗幹喜曰：「是吾志也。」

translations.literal: Zonggan said with delight, "That is my intent as well."
translations.idiomatic: Zonggan said with delight, "That has long been my intent."

sentences.zh: 即除參知行台尚書省事。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed Acting Commissioner of the Branch Secretariat of the Regional Command.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed Acting Commissioner of the Branch Secretariat at the Regional Command.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔宗弼複取河南，通古請先行至汴諭之。

translations.literal: Before long, an edict ordered Zongbi to recover Henan again; Tonggu asked to go ahead first to Bian and announce this.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, an edict ordered Zongbi to retake Henan; Tonggu asked to go ahead to Bian first and deliver the message.

sentences.zh: 比至汴，宋人已去矣。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Bian, the Song forces had already withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Bian, the Song forces had already withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 或謂通古曰：「宋人先退，詐也，今聞將自許、宿來襲我。」

translations.literal: Someone said to Tonggu, "The Song withdrew first as a ruse; it is now heard that they will attack us from Xu and Su."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Tonggu, "The Song withdrawal was a feint; we now hear they will strike from Xu and Su prefectures."

sentences.zh: 通古曰：「南人宣言來者，正所以走耳。」

translations.literal: Tonggu said, "When southerners announce they are coming, that is precisely how they make their escape."
translations.idiomatic: Tonggu said, "When southerners announce they are coming, that is exactly how they cover a retreat."

sentences.zh: 乃使人覘之，宋人果潰去。

translations.literal: He then sent men to scout, and the Song forces indeed broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He sent scouts, and the Song forces had indeed broken and fled.

sentences.zh: 宗弼撫髀笑曰：「誰謂書生不能曉兵事哉？」

translations.literal: Zongbi slapped his thigh and laughed, saying, "Who says a scholar cannot understand military affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi slapped his thigh and laughed. "Who says a scholar cannot understand war?"

sentences.zh: 河南卒孫進詐稱「皇弟按察大王」，謀作亂。

translations.literal: A Henan soldier named Sun Jin falsely claimed to be "the Imperial Younger Brother, Investigating Grand Prince" and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: A Henan soldier named Sun Jin falsely claimed to be "the emperor's younger brother, the Investigating Grand Prince" and plotted a revolt.

sentences.zh: 是時海陵為相，內懷覬覦，欲先除熙宗弟胙王常勝，因孫進稱皇弟大王，遂指名為胙王以誣構之。

translations.literal: At this time Hailing was Chancellor; inwardly he harbored ambition and wished first to eliminate Emperor Xizong's younger brother Prince Zuowang Changsheng; because Sun Jin had claimed to be the Imperial Younger Brother Grand Prince, he therefore named Zuowang to frame him.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Prince Hailing was Chancellor; he already coveted the throne and wished first to eliminate Emperor Xizong's younger brother, Prince Zuowang Changsheng. Because Sun Jin had claimed to be the imperial younger brother and grand prince, Hailing named Zuowang as the culprit and framed him.

sentences.zh: 熙宗自太子濟安薨後，繼嗣未定，深以為念。

translations.literal: Since Crown Prince Ji'an died, Emperor Xizong's succession was unsettled, and he brooded deeply over this.
translations.idiomatic: Since Crown Prince Ji'an's death, Emperor Xizong had no settled heir, and the matter weighed heavily on his mind.

sentences.zh: 裴滿後多專制，不得肆意後宮，頗鬱鬱，因縱酒，往往迷惑妄怒，手刃殺人。

translations.literal: Empress Pusan was domineering; he could not indulge freely in the inner palace, grew quite depressed, and so gave himself to drink, often becoming confused and rashly angry and killing men with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Pusan was domineering, and he could not have his way in the inner palace; he grew depressed, drank heavily, and in drunken confusion would fly into rage and kill men with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 及海陵中傷胙王，熙宗以為信然不疑，遣護衛特思就汴京鞫治。

translations.literal: When Hailing slandered Prince Zuowang, Emperor Xizong believed it without doubt and sent the guardsman Tesi to Bianjing to investigate and try the case.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing slandered Prince Zuowang, Emperor Xizong believed it without question and sent the guardsman Tesi to Bianjing to investigate.

sentences.zh: 行台知熙宗意在胙王，導引孫進連屬之。

translations.literal: The Regional Command knew the emperor's mind was set on Prince Zuowang and guided Sun Jin to implicate him in a chain of association.
translations.idiomatic: The Regional Command knew the emperor's mind was fixed on Prince Zuowang and steered Sun Jin's testimony to implicate him.

sentences.zh: 通古執其咎，極力辯止。

translations.literal: Tonggu seized on the fault in this and argued strenuously to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Tonggu seized on the flaw in the case and argued strenuously to stop it.

sentences.zh: 及孫進引服，蓋假託名稱，將以惑眾，規取財物耳，實無其人也。

translations.literal: When Sun Jin confessed, it turned out he had only borrowed a title to deceive the crowd and scheme for goods and wealth—there was in fact no such person.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jin confessed, it emerged that he had only borrowed a grand title to deceive the crowd and extort wealth—no such prince existed at all.

sentences.zh: 特思奏狀，海陵譖之曰：「特思且將徼福于胙王。」

translations.literal: Tesi submitted his report; Hailing slandered him, saying, "Tesi is even now seeking favor from Prince Zuowang."
translations.idiomatic: Tesi submitted his report; Hailing slandered him, saying, "Tesi is even now currying favor with Prince Zuowang."

sentences.zh: 熙宗益以海陵為信，遂殺胙王，並特思殺之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong trusted Hailing all the more, and so killed Prince Zuowang and killed Tesi as well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted Hailing all the more, had Prince Zuowang killed, and killed Tesi as well.

sentences.zh: 行台諸人乃責通古曰：「為君所誤，今坐死矣。」

translations.literal: The men of the Regional Command then reproached Tonggu, saying, "Misled by you, we now face death as accomplices."
translations.idiomatic: The Regional Command officials then reproached Tonggu: "You misled us—we now face death as accomplices."

sentences.zh: 通古曰：「以正獲罪死，賢於生。」

translations.literal: Tonggu said, "To die punished for upholding what is right is better than to live."
translations.idiomatic: Tonggu said, "To die punished for doing what is right is better than living in disgrace."

sentences.zh: 海陵既殺胙王，不復緣害他人，由是坐止特思，行台不坐。

translations.literal: Once Hailing had killed Prince Zuowang, he did not pursue harm against the others; thus only Tesi was punished by law, and the Regional Command was not implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hailing had killed Prince Zuowang, he did not pursue the others; only Tesi was punished, and the Regional Command was spared.

sentences.zh: 天德初，遷行台左丞，進拜平章政事，封譚王，改封鄆王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande, he was transferred to Left Vice Commissioner of the Regional Command, advanced to Grand Councilor, enfeoffed as Prince of Tan, and later changed to Prince of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tiande era, he was made Left Vice Commissioner of the Regional Command, then Grand Councilor, enfeoffed as Prince of Tan, and later as Prince of Yun.

sentences.zh: 以疾求解機務，不許。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he asked to be relieved of state affairs; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to be relieved of state affairs on grounds of illness, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 拜司徒，封沈王。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Mentor and enfeoffed as Prince of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Mentor and enfeoffed as Prince of Shen.

sentences.zh: 海陵禦下嚴厲，收威柄，親王大臣未嘗少假以顏色，惟見通古，必以禮貌。

translations.literal: Hailing was stern toward his subordinates and gathered power into his own hands; imperial princes and great ministers never received even a little pleasant countenance from him—only when he saw Tonggu did he always show courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing ruled his subordinates with severity and kept power tightly in hand; princes and great ministers rarely saw even a trace of warmth from him—only toward Tonggu did he always show courtesy.

sentences.zh: 會磁州僧法寶欲去，張浩、張暉欲留之不可得，朝官又有欲留之者。

translations.literal: It happened that the monk Fabao of Cizhou wished to leave; Zhang Hao and Zhang Hui wished to keep him but could not, and there were also court officials who wished to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the monk Fabao of Cizhou wished to leave; Zhang Hao and Zhang Hui tried to keep him but could not, and other court officials also wanted him to stay.

sentences.zh: 海陵聞其事，詔三品以上官上殿，責之曰：「聞卿等每到寺，僧法寶正坐，卿等皆坐其側，朕甚不取。

translations.literal: Hailing heard of the matter and ordered officials of the third rank and above to come before the throne, rebuking them: "I hear that whenever you go to the temple, the monk Fabao sits in the central seat while you all sit at his side—this I greatly disapprove.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing heard of it and summoned officials of the third rank and above, rebuking them: "I hear that whenever you visit the temple, the monk Fabao sits in the place of honor while you sit at his side—I find this unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 佛者本一小國王子，能輕舍富貴，自苦修行，由是成佛，今人崇敬。

translations.literal: The Buddha was originally a prince of a small state who could lightly abandon wealth and honor, afflict himself in practice, and thereby become a Buddha; people today revere him.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha was once a prince of a small kingdom who willingly gave up wealth and rank, disciplined himself in hardship, and thereby attained enlightenment—hence the reverence he receives today.

sentences.zh: 以希福利，皆妄也。

translations.literal: To seek blessings and profit through him is all delusion.
translations.idiomatic: To seek blessings and profit from him is mere delusion.

sentences.zh: 況僧者，往往不第秀才，市井游食，生計不足，乃去為僧，較其貴賤，未可與簿尉抗禮。

translations.literal: Moreover, monks are often failed examination candidates and marketplace drifters who, when livelihood fails, go off to become monks; compared in rank and status, they may not stand on equal ritual footing with clerks and assistant magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, monks are often failed examination candidates and marketplace drifters who turn to the cloth when they cannot make a living; in rank they are not fit to receive the same ceremonial treatment as clerks and assistant magistrates.

sentences.zh: 閭閻老婦，迫於死期，多歸信之。

translations.literal: Old women in the lanes and alleys, pressed by the approach of death, mostly put their faith in them.
translations.idiomatic: Old women in the lanes, facing death, mostly put their faith in them.

sentences.zh: 卿等位為宰輔，乃複效此，失大臣體。

translations.literal: You hold the rank of chief ministers, yet you again imitate this—this falls short of the bearing proper to great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: You hold the rank of chief ministers, yet you imitate this—it is unworthy of your station.

sentences.zh: 張司徒老成舊人，三教該通，足為儀錶，何不師之？」

translations.literal: Grand Mentor Zhang is a seasoned elder who has mastered all three teachings and is fit to serve as a model—why not take him as your teacher?"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Mentor Zhang is a seasoned elder versed in all three teachings and fit to serve as your model—why not learn from him?"

sentences.zh: 召法寶謂之曰：「汝既為僧，去住在己，何乃使人知之？」

translations.literal: He summoned Fabao and said to him, "Since you are a monk, whether you stay or go is your own affair—why let others know of it?"
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Fabao and said, "You are a monk—whether you stay or go is your own affair. Why let the court know of it?"

sentences.zh: 法寶戰懼，不知所為。

translations.literal: Fabao trembled in fear and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Fabao trembled in fear and did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「汝為長老，當有定力，今乃畏死耶？」

translations.literal: Hailing said, "You are an elder of the community and ought to have firm resolve—are you now afraid of death?"
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "You are a senior monk and ought to have firm resolve—are you afraid of death now?"

sentences.zh: 遂於朝堂杖之二百，張浩、張暉杖二十。

translations.literal: He then had him beaten two hundred strokes in the court hall; Zhang Hao and Zhang Hui were beaten twenty strokes each.
translations.idiomatic: He had Fabao beaten two hundred strokes in the court hall; Zhang Hao and Zhang Hui received twenty strokes each.

sentences.zh: 正隆元年，以司徒致仕，進封曹王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenglong he retired as Grand Mentor and was advanced in enfeoffment to Prince of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 1 he retired as grand mentor and was promoted to Prince of Cao.

sentences.zh: 是年，薨，年六十九。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died, aged sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 通古天資樂易，不為表襮，雖居宰相，自奉如寒素焉。

translations.literal: Tonggu was by nature cheerful and easygoing and made no outward display; though he held the rank of chief minister, he maintained himself as if in humble poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Tonggu was by nature cheerful and unpretentious; though he held the rank of chief minister, he lived as simply as a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 子沉，天德三年，賜楊建中榜及第。

translations.literal: His son Chen, in the third year of Tiande, was granted graduation on the Yang Jianzhong examination list.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chen passed the examinations in the third year of Tiande on the Yang Jianzhong list.

sentences.zh: 張浩，字浩然，遼陽渤海人。

translations.literal: Zhang Hao, style name Haoran, was a man of Bohai in Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao, whose style name was Haoran, came from the Bohai community in Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 本姓高，東明王之後。

translations.literal: His original surname was Gao; he was a descendant of the King of Dongming.
translations.idiomatic: His family had originally borne the surname Gao and descended from the King of Dongming.

sentences.zh: 曾祖霸，仕遼而為張氏。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Ba served Liao and became of the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Ba served the Liao and took the surname Zhang.

sentences.zh: 天輔中，遼東平，浩以策幹太祖，太祖以浩為承應御前文字。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu period, when eastern Liao was pacified, Hao presented a stratagem to win over Taizu, and Taizu appointed Hao to handle documents before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era, when eastern Liao was pacified, Hao won Taizu's attention with a policy proposal and was appointed to handle documents before the throne.

sentences.zh: 天會八年，賜進士及第，授秘書郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianhui he was granted jinshi status and appointed Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianhui (1130) he received his jinshi degree and was appointed Secretary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 太宗將幸東京，浩提點繕修大內，超遷衛尉卿，權簽宣徽院事，管勾御前文字，初定朝儀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong was about to visit the Eastern Capital, Hao supervised repairs to the inner palace, was promoted out of turn to Minister of the Court for the Imperial Clan, acted as provisional signatory of the Palace Domestic Service, managed documents before the throne, and first established court ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong was about to visit the Eastern Capital, Hao supervised repairs to the inner palace, was promoted out of turn to Minister of the Court for the Imperial Clan, acted as provisional signatory of the Palace Domestic Service, managed documents before the throne, and first established court ritual.

sentences.zh: 求養親，去職。

translations.literal: He asked to care for his parents and left office.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to care for his parents and resigned his post.

sentences.zh: 起為趙州刺史。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed Prefect of Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed prefect of Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 官制行，以中大夫為大理卿。

translations.literal: When the official system was implemented, he served as Grand Master of the Palace and Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When the new official system took effect, he served as Grand Master of the Palace and Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 天眷二年，詳定內外儀式，曆戶、工、禮三部侍郎，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjuan he worked out inner and outer ceremonial forms in detail, passed through the vice ministries of Revenue, Works, and Rites, and was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjuan (1138) he codified inner and outer ceremonial forms, served successively as vice minister of Revenue, Works, and Rites, and was promoted to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 田玨黨事起，台省一空，以浩行六部事。

translations.literal: When the Tian Jue faction affair arose, the censorate and secretariat were emptied out, and Hao handled the affairs of all six ministries.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tian Jue faction affair broke, the censorate and secretariat were emptied out, and Hao was put in charge of all six ministries.

sentences.zh: 簿書叢委，決遣無留，人服其才。

translations.literal: Documents piled up in heaps, yet he decided and dispatched without delay; people admired his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Documents piled up in heaps, yet he decided and dispatched without delay; people admired his ability.

sentences.zh: 以疾求外，補除彰德軍節度使，遷燕京路都轉運使。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he sought an outside post and was appointed Military Commissioner of Zhangde Army; he was then transferred to Director-General of Transport for the Yanjing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On grounds of illness he sought a provincial post and was appointed military commissioner of Zhangde Army, then director-general of transport for the Yanjing circuit.

sentences.zh: 俄改平陽尹。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Prefect of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed prefect of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 平陽多盜，臨汾男子夜掠人婦，浩捕得，榜殺之，盜遂衰息。

translations.literal: Pingyang had many bandits; a man of Linfen robbed a woman by night, and when Hao captured him he had him exposed and killed on the placard, after which banditry declined and ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyang had many bandits; when Hao captured a Linfen man who had robbed a woman by night, he had him publicly executed, and banditry soon subsided.

sentences.zh: 近郊有淫祠，郡人頗事之。

translations.literal: In the suburbs there was an illicit shrine, and the people of the commandery largely worshipped at it.
translations.idiomatic: In the suburbs there was an illicit shrine that many in the prefecture patronized.

sentences.zh: 廟祝、田主爭香火之利，累年不決。

translations.literal: The temple acolyte and the field-holder disputed the profits of offerings and incense, and for years no settlement was reached.
translations.idiomatic: The temple acolyte and the field-holder disputed the profits from offerings and incense, and for years the case went unresolved.

sentences.zh: 浩撤其祠屋，投其像水中。

translations.literal: Hao demolished the shrine buildings and cast its images into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Hao demolished the shrine and cast its images into the water.

sentences.zh: 強宗黠吏屏跡，莫敢犯者。

translations.literal: Powerful clans and crafty clerks withdrew from sight, and none dared offend.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful clans and crafty clerks withdrew from sight, and none dared offend.

sentences.zh: 郡中大治。

translations.literal: The commandery was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was brought to excellent order.

sentences.zh: 乃繕葺堯帝祠，作擊壤遺風亭。

translations.literal: He then repaired the shrine of Emperor Yao and built the Pavilion of the Surviving Custom of Beating the Earth.
translations.idiomatic: He then repaired the shrine of Emperor Yao and built the Pavilion of the Surviving Custom of Beating the Earth.

sentences.zh: 海陵召為戶部尚書，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Hailing summoned him as Minister of Revenue and appointed him Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing summoned him as Minister of Revenue and appointed him Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiande he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 起複參知政事，進拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning, he resumed as Vice Grand Councilor and was advanced to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning, he resumed as Vice Grand Councilor and was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 天德三年，廣燕京城，營建宮室。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiande the Yanjing city walls were expanded and palace buildings were constructed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiande the walls of Yanjing were expanded and palace buildings were constructed.

sentences.zh: 浩與燕京留守劉筈、大名尹盧彥倫監護工作，命浩就擬差除。

translations.literal: Hao, together with the Yanjing Military Commissioner Liu Qia and the Prefect of Daming Lu Yanlun, supervised the work; Hao was ordered to propose appointments on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, together with the Yanjing military commissioner Liu Qia and the prefect of Daming Lu Yanlun, supervised the work, and Hao was authorized to propose appointments on the spot.

sentences.zh: 既而暑月，工役多疾疫。

translations.literal: Before long, in the hot summer months, many laborers fell ill with epidemic disease.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, in the hot summer months, many laborers fell ill with epidemic disease.

sentences.zh: 詔發燕京五百里內醫者，使治療，官給藥物，全活多者與官，其次給賞，下者轉運司舉察以聞。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched physicians within five hundred li of Yanjing to treat them, with medicines supplied by the state; those who saved many lives were granted office, the next rank received rewards, and the lowest were to be investigated and reported by the transport commission.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched physicians within five hundred li of Yanjing to treat them, with medicines supplied by the state; those who saved many lives were granted office, the next rank received rewards, and the lowest were to be investigated and reported by the transport commission.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，海陵定都燕京，改燕京為中都，改析津府為大興府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, Hailing fixed the capital at Yanjing, changed Yanjing to the Central Capital, and changed Xizhi Prefecture to Daxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 1 Hailing made Yanjing the capital, renamed it the Central Capital, and changed Xizhi Prefecture to Daxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 浩進拜平章政事，賜金帶玉帶各一，賜宴于魚藻池。

translations.literal: Hao was advanced to Grand Councilor, was granted one golden belt and one jade belt, and was given a banquet at the Fish-Algae Pool.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was promoted to grand councilor, granted a golden belt and a jade belt, and entertained at the Fish-Algae Pool.

sentences.zh: 浩請凡四方之民欲居中都者，給複十年，以實京城，從之。

translations.literal: Hao requested that for all people from the four quarters who wished to reside in the Central Capital, ten years of tax exemption be granted to fill the capital city; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Hao asked that commoners from all regions who wished to settle in the Central Capital be granted ten years of tax exemption to fill the city, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 拜尚書右丞相兼侍中，封潞王，賜其子汝霖進士及第。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Chief Councillor of the Secretariat, concurrently Palace Attendant, enfeoffed as Prince of Lu, and his son Rulin was granted the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed right chief councillor of the Secretariat, concurrently palace attendant, enfeoffed as Prince of Lu, and his son Rulin was granted the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改封蜀王，進拜左丞相。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred in enfeoffment to Prince of Shu and advanced to Left Chief Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reassigned as Prince of Shu and promoted to left chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，改封魯國公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong he was transferred in enfeoffment to Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 2 he was reassigned as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「人君不明，諫不行，言不聽，則宰相求去。

translations.literal: Hailing said: "When a ruler is unenlightened, remonstrance is not followed, and words are not heeded, then the chief minister seeks to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "When a ruler is unenlightened, remonstrance goes unheeded and counsel unheard, the chief minister seeks to leave office.

sentences.zh: 宰相老病不能任事則求去。

translations.literal: When the chief minister is old and ill and cannot bear office, he seeks to leave.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief minister is old and ill and cannot bear office, he seeks to leave.

sentences.zh: 卿于二者何居？」

translations.literal: Between these two cases, where do you stand?"
translations.idiomatic: Which of these two cases applies to you?"

sentences.zh: 浩對曰：「臣羸病不堪任事，宰相非養病之地也，是以求去。」

translations.literal: Hao replied: "Your servant is frail and ill and cannot bear office; the chief ministership is no place to convalesce, and therefore I seek to leave."
translations.idiomatic: Hao answered, "I am frail and ill and cannot bear office; the chief ministership is no place to convalesce, and that is why I seek to leave."

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: Permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 海陵欲伐宋，將幸汴，而汴京大內失火，於是使浩與敬嗣暉營建南京宮室。

translations.literal: Hailing wished to attack Song and was about to visit Bian, but the inner palace at Bianjing caught fire; he therefore had Hao and Jing Sihui construct the palace buildings of the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing planned to attack Song and was about to visit Bian, but fire destroyed the inner palace at Bianjing; he therefore put Hao and Jing Sihui in charge of building the Southern Capital palaces.

sentences.zh: 浩從容奏曰：「往歲營治中都，天下樂然趨之。

translations.literal: Hao calmly memorialized, saying, "In former years when the Central Capital was built and put in order, all under Heaven gladly rushed to take part.
translations.idiomatic: Hao calmly memorialized, "When the Central Capital was built in former years, the realm gladly rallied to the work.

sentences.zh: 今民力未複，而重勞之，恐不似前時之易成也。」

translations.literal: Now the people's strength has not yet recovered, and if we burden them again, I fear it will not be as easy to complete as before."
translations.idiomatic: The people's strength has not yet recovered; if we burden them again, I fear the work will not be completed as easily as before."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: His advice was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 浩朝辭，海陵問用兵利害。

translations.literal: When Hao took leave at court, Hailing asked about the advantages and disadvantages of using troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao took leave at court, Hailing asked about the advantages and disadvantages of going to war.

sentences.zh: 浩不敢正諫，乃婉詞以對，欲以微止海陵用兵，奏曰：「臣觀天意，欲絕趙氏久矣。」

translations.literal: Hao did not dare remonstrate directly; he answered in indirect language, wishing thereby in a slight way to stop Hailing from using troops, and memorialized, saying, "Your servant observes that Heaven's will has long been to extinguish the House of Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: Hao did not dare speak bluntly; he answered in guarded terms, hoping in a small way to dissuade Hailing from going to war, and memorialized, "I observe that Heaven has long intended to end the Zhao line."

sentences.zh: 海陵愕然曰：「何以知之？」

translations.literal: Hailing said in astonishment, "How do you know this?"
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was startled. "How do you know that?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「趙構無子，樹立疏屬，其勢必生變，可不煩用兵而服之。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Zhao Gou has no son; if a distant kinsman is set up, change is bound to arise—Song can be brought to submit without troubling to use troops."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Zhao Gou has no heir; if a distant collateral is enthroned, turmoil is sure to follow, and the Song can be brought to heel without the trouble of war."

sentences.zh: 海陵雖喜其言，而不能從也。

translations.literal: Although Hailing was pleased with his words, he could not follow them.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was pleased with what he heard, but he would not act on it.

sentences.zh: 浩至汴，海陵時時使宦者梁珫來視工役，凡一殿之成，費累巨萬。

translations.literal: When Hao reached Bian, Hailing repeatedly sent the eunuch Liang Chong to inspect the labor; for each hall completed, the cost ran to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao arrived at Bian, Hailing repeatedly sent the eunuch Liang Chong to inspect the work; the completion of a single hall cost vast sums.

sentences.zh: 珫指曰：「某處不如法式。」

translations.literal: Chong would point and say, "Such-and-such a place does not accord with the standard pattern."
translations.idiomatic: Chong would point and say, "This part does not meet the prescribed form."

sentences.zh: 輒撤之。

translations.literal: and it would at once be torn down.
translations.idiomatic: Chong would have it torn down at once.

sentences.zh: 浩不能抗而與之均禮。

translations.literal: Hao could not resist him and treated him with equal ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Hao could not stand up to him and accorded him equal ritual standing.

sentences.zh: 汴宮成，海陵自燕來遷居之。

translations.literal: When the Bian palace was completed, Hailing came from Yan to move his residence there.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bian palace was finished, Hailing came from Yan to take up residence there.

sentences.zh: 浩拜太傅、尚書令，進封秦國公。

translations.literal: Hao was appointed Grand Tutor and Director of the Department of State Affairs, and was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was appointed Grand Tutor and Director of the Department of State Affairs and was further enfeoffed as Duke of Qin.

sentences.zh: 海陵至汴，累月不視朝，日治兵南伐，部署諸將。

translations.literal: After Hailing reached Bian, for many months he did not hold court, but daily drilled troops for the southern campaign and deployed the generals.
translations.idiomatic: After Hailing reached Bian, he went months without holding court, drilling troops daily for the southern campaign and deploying his generals.

sentences.zh: 浩欲奏事，不得見。

translations.literal: Hao wished to memorialize on affairs but could not obtain an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Hao wished to present memorials on state affairs but could not gain an audience.

sentences.zh: 會海陵遣周福兒至浩家，浩附奏曰：「諸將皆新進少年，恐誤國事。

translations.literal: It happened that Hailing sent Zhou Fu'er to Hao's house; Hao attached a memorial, saying, "The generals are all newly advanced young men; I fear they will mishandle state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing sent Zhou Fu'er to Hao's house, Hao attached a memorial: "The generals are all newly promoted youths; I fear they will mishandle state affairs.

sentences.zh: 宜求舊人練習兵者，以為千戶謀克。」

translations.literal: It would be fitting to seek old men practiced in warfare and appoint them as thousand-household leaders and company commanders."
translations.idiomatic: You should seek veterans skilled in warfare and appoint them as thousand-household leaders and company commanders."

sentences.zh: 而海陵部署已定，惡聞其言，乃杖之。

translations.literal: But Hailing's deployments were already settled; he hated to hear such words and had Hao beaten with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: But Hailing had already fixed his deployments; he hated to hear this and had Hao beaten with the staff.

sentences.zh: 海陵自將發汴京，皇后、太子居守。

translations.literal: Hailing himself was to lead the army out from Bianjing; the empress and crown prince remained to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was to lead the army out from Bianjing himself, while the empress and crown prince stayed behind to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 浩留治尚書省事。

translations.literal: Hao remained to administer the affairs of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hao remained behind to administer the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位于遼陽，揚州軍變，海陵遇害。

translations.literal: Shizong took the throne at Liaoyang; the army at Yangzhou mutinied, and Hailing was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong took the throne at Liaoyang; the army at Yangzhou mutinied, and Hailing was assassinated.

sentences.zh: 都督府使使殺太子光英于南京。

translations.literal: The military governor's envoy killed the crown prince Guang Ying at the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy of the military governor killed Crown Prince Guang Ying at the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 浩遣戶部員外郎完顏謀衍上賀表。

translations.literal: Hao sent Wanyan Mouyan of the Ministry of Revenue, an outer-office official, to present a congratulatory memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Hao sent Wanyan Mouyan, an outer-office official of the Ministry of Revenue, to present a congratulatory memorial.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，浩朝京師，入見。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, Hao came to court at the capital and was received in audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year, Hao came to the capital for court and was received in audience.

sentences.zh: 世宗謂曰：「朕思天位惟艱，夙夜惕懼，不遑寧處。

translations.literal: Shizong said to him, "I reflect that the throne is hard to hold; morning and night I am vigilant and fearful, without leisure to rest at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong said to him, "I reflect that the throne is hard to hold; day and night I am vigilant and afraid, with no leisure to rest easy.

sentences.zh: 卿國之元老，當戮力贊治，宜令後世稱揚德政，毋失委注之意也。」

translations.literal: You are an elder statesman of the realm; you should exert your strength to assist in governing, so that later ages may praise your virtuous administration and you do not fail the trust placed in you."
translations.idiomatic: You are an elder of the state; exert yourself to help govern, so that posterity may praise your virtuous rule and you do not betray the trust I place in you."

sentences.zh: 俄拜太師、尚書令，封南陽郡王。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed Grand Preceptor and Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed Grand Preceptor and Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 世宗曰：「卿在正隆時為首相，不能匡救，惡得無罪。

translations.literal: Shizong said, "In the Zhenlong era you were chief minister; you could not rescue the situation—how can you be without guilt?
translations.idiomatic: Shizong said, "In the Zhenlong era you were chief minister and could not set things right—how can you be without fault?

sentences.zh: 營建兩宮，殫竭民力，汝亦嘗諫，故天下不以咎汝，惟怨正隆。

translations.literal: In building the two palaces the people's strength was exhausted; you also remonstrated, so all under Heaven does not blame you but only resents Zhenlong.
translations.idiomatic: Building the two palaces exhausted the people; you did remonstrate, so the realm does not blame you but only resents the Zhenlong reign.

sentences.zh: 而卿在省十餘年，練達政務，故複用卿為相，當自勉，毋負朕意。」

translations.literal: Yet you served in the Secretariat for more than ten years and are thoroughly versed in government affairs; therefore I employ you again as chancellor. You should encourage yourself and not fail my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Yet you served in the Secretariat for more than ten years and know government affairs well; that is why I employ you again as chancellor. Exert yourself and do not betray my intent."

sentences.zh: 浩頓首謝。

translations.literal: Hao bowed his head to the ground in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Hao kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 居數日，世宗謂浩曰：「卿為尚書令，凡人材有可用者，當舉用之。」

translations.literal: After several days, Shizong said to Hao, "As Director of the Department of State Affairs, whenever there is talent that can be used, you should recommend and employ it."
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Shizong told Hao, "As Director of the Department of State Affairs, whenever you find usable talent, you should recommend and appoint it."

sentences.zh: 浩舉紇石烈志寧等，其後皆為名臣。

translations.literal: Hao recommended Heshilie Zhining and others; afterward they all became famous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Hao recommended Heshilie Zhining and others; they all later became renowned ministers.

sentences.zh: 浩有疾，在告者久之。

translations.literal: Hao fell ill and was on leave of absence for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Hao fell ill and was on extended sick leave.

sentences.zh: 遣左司郎中高衎及浩侄汝弼宣諭。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Left Department Director Gao Kan and Hao's nephew Rubi to convey imperial instructions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Left Department Director Gao Kan and Hao's nephew Zhang Rubi to convey his instructions.

sentences.zh: 浩力疾入對，即詔入朝毋拜，許設座殿陛之東，若有咨謀，然後進對。

translations.literal: Hao forced himself, though ill, to enter for audience; at once an edict ordered that on entering court he need not bow, and permitted a seat to be set east of the palace steps; only when there was consultation was he then to advance for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Hao dragged himself in despite his illness; the court at once ordered that he need not bow on entering, granted him a seat east of the palace steps, and required him to advance for audience only when consultation was needed.

sentences.zh: 或體中不佳，不必日至省中，大政可就第裁決。

translations.literal: If his health was not good, he need not come daily to the Secretariat; great affairs might be decided at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: If he was unwell, he need not come to the Secretariat every day; major affairs could be decided at his home.

sentences.zh: 浩雖受詔，然每以退為請。

translations.literal: Although Hao received the edict, he repeatedly asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Though Hao accepted the edict, he repeatedly asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，複申前請。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year he again submitted his former request.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year he renewed his earlier request.

sentences.zh: 乃除判東京留守。

translations.literal: He was then appointed acting military governor of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed acting military governor of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 疾不能赴任，因請致仕。

translations.literal: His illness prevented him from taking up the post, and he therefore requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Illness kept him from taking up the post, and he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 初，近侍有欲罷科舉者，上曰：「吾見太師議之。」

translations.literal: Earlier, a close attendant had wished to abolish the civil-service examinations; the emperor said, "I shall see what the Grand Preceptor says on the matter."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a close attendant had wanted to abolish the civil-service examinations; the emperor said, "I will hear what the Grand Preceptor has to say."

sentences.zh: 浩入見，上曰：「自古帝王有不用文學者乎？」

translations.literal: When Hao entered for audience, the emperor said, "From antiquity, has there ever been an emperor who did not employ literary learning?"
translations.idiomatic: When Hao came in for audience, the emperor asked, "Has there ever been an emperor who dispensed with literary learning?"

sentences.zh: 浩對曰：「有。」

translations.literal: Hao replied, "There has."
translations.idiomatic: Hao answered, "There has."

sentences.zh: 曰：「誰歟？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Who was it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Who?"

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「秦始皇。」

translations.literal: Hao said, "Qin Shihuang."
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Qin Shihuang."

sentences.zh: 上顧左右曰：「豈可使我為始皇乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor turned to those beside him and said, "How could I be made another First Emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to his attendants and said, "Am I to be another First Emperor!"

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was thereupon dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 是歲，薨。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died.

sentences.zh: 上輟朝一日。

translations.literal: The emperor suspended court for one day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended court for one day.

sentences.zh: 詔左宣徽使趙興祥率百官致奠，賻銀千兩、重彩五十端、絹五百匹。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Left Palace Attendant Zhao Xingxiang to lead the hundred officials in offering condolences, with funeral gifts of a thousand taels of silver, fifty bolts of fine colored silks, and five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Left Palace Attendant Zhao Xingxiang to lead the officials in offering condolences, with funeral gifts of a thousand taels of silver, fifty bolts of fine colored silk, and five hundred bolts of plain silk.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文康。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Wenkang.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Wenkang.

sentences.zh: 明昌五年，配享世宗廟廷。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Mingchang he was given a place in Shizong's temple sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Mingchang he was granted a place in the sacrifices at Shizong's temple.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年，圖像衍慶宮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe his portrait was placed in Yansqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taihe his portrait was placed in Yansqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 子汝為、汝霖、汝能、汝方、汝猷。

translations.literal: His sons were Ruwei, Rulin, Runeng, Rufang, and Ruyou.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Ruwei, Rulin, Runeng, Rufang, and Ruyou.

sentences.zh: 子 汝霖

translations.literal: Son: Rulin
translations.idiomatic: His son Rulin

sentences.zh: 汝霖字仲澤，少聰慧好學，浩嘗稱之曰：「吾家千里駒也。」

translations.literal: Rulin, style name Zhongze, in youth was clever and fond of learning; Hao once praised him, saying, "He is the thousand-li colt of our house."
translations.idiomatic: Rulin, whose style name was Zhongze, was clever and studious from youth; Hao once said of him, "He is the thousand-li steed of our house."

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，賜呂忠翰榜下進士第，特授左補闕，擢大興縣令，再遷禮部員外郎、翰林待制。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan he was granted the jinshi degree below Lü Zhonghan on the list, was specially appointed Left Remonstrator, was promoted to magistrate of Daxing County, and was twice transferred to Outer-office Director of the Ministry of Rites and Hanlin Academician-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyuan he was granted the jinshi degree immediately below Lü Zhonghan on the examination list, was specially appointed Left Remonstrator, became magistrate of Daxing County, and was twice promoted to Outer-office Director of the Ministry of Rites and Hanlin Academician-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 大定八年，除刑部郎中，召見于香閣，諭之曰：「卿以待制除郎中，勿以為降。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dading he was appointed Director of the Ministry of Punishments; summoned to audience in the Fragrant Pavilion, the emperor instructed him, saying, "You are being made director from the post of academician-in-waiting—do not regard it as a demotion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dading he was appointed Director of the Ministry of Punishments; summoned to audience in the Fragrant Pavilion, the emperor told him, "You are being moved from academician-in-waiting to director—do not take it as a demotion.

sentences.zh: 朕以刑部闕漢官，故以授卿。

translations.literal: Because the Ministry of Punishments lacks Han officials, I therefore confer it on you.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Punishments lacks Han officials, which is why I am giving you the post.

sentences.zh: 且卿入仕未久，姑試其能耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, you have not long entered office; for the present I am merely testing your ability.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, you have not been in office long; for now I am only testing what you can do.

sentences.zh: 如職事修舉，當有升擢。

translations.literal: If your duties are well performed, there will be promotion.
translations.idiomatic: If you discharge your duties well, you will be promoted.

sentences.zh: 爾父太師以戶部尚書升諸相位，由崇德大夫躐遷金紫，卿所自見也。

translations.literal: Your father the Grand Preceptor rose from Minister of Revenue to the rank of chancellor, leaping from Chongde Grand Master to Golden Purple; you have seen it yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Your father the Grand Preceptor rose from Minister of Revenue to chancellor, leaping from Chongde Grand Master to Golden Purple rank—you have seen it with your own eyes.

sentences.zh: 當既厥心，無忝乃父。」

translations.literal: You should fulfill your heart's intent and not disgrace your father."
translations.idiomatic: Give your whole heart to the task and do not disgrace your father."

sentences.zh: 明年，授太子左諭德兼禮部郎中。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Left Tutor of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Outer-office Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Left Tutor of the Heir Apparent, while retaining the concurrent post of Outer-office Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 先是，知登聞檢院王震改禮部郎中，世宗諭宰臣曰：「此除未允人望，禮官當選有學術士，如張汝霖者可也。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Zhen, who knew the Petition Office for Hearing Grievances, was transferred to Outer-office Director of the Ministry of Rites; Shizong instructed the chief ministers, saying, "This appointment does not satisfy public expectation; for a ritual official one should select a man of learning, such as Zhang Rulin."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Zhen, director of the Petition Office for Hearing Grievances, had been transferred to Outer-office Director of the Ministry of Rites; Shizong told the chief ministers, "This appointment does not satisfy public expectation; a ritual post should go to a learned man, such as Zhang Rulin."

sentences.zh: 於是，命汝霖兼之而除震別職。

translations.literal: Thereupon Rulin was ordered to hold the post concurrently while Wang Zhen was given another appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Rulin was then ordered to hold the post concurrently while Wang Zhen was reassigned.

sentences.zh: 擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 以憂解，起複為太子詹事，遷太子少師兼禦史中丞。

translations.literal: He left office on mourning, then was recalled and made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and was transferred to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning, then was recalled as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, concurrently serving as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 世宗召謂曰：「卿嘗言，監察禦史所察州縣官多因沽買以得名譽，良吏奉法不為表襮，必無所稱。

translations.literal: Shizong summoned him and said, "You once said that the investigating censors, in investigating prefectural and county officials, often gain reputation through purchases and sales, while good officials who uphold the law and do not show off necessarily receive no praise.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong summoned him and said, "You once observed that investigating censors often win reputation for county and prefectural officials through trading favors, while good officials who simply uphold the law and make no display go unrecommended.

sentences.zh: 朕意亦然。

translations.literal: My mind is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: I feel the same.

sentences.zh: 卿今為台官，可革其弊。」

translations.literal: Now that you are a censorial official, you may reform this abuse."
translations.idiomatic: Now that you head the Censorate, you can reform this abuse."

sentences.zh: 尋改中都路都轉運使、太子少師兼禮部尚書，俄轉吏部，為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Metropolitan Transport Commissioner of the Zhongdu Circuit, Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent concurrently Minister of Rites, soon transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made Metropolitan Transport Commissioner of the Zhongdu Circuit, Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent concurrently Minister of Rites, then transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時將陵主簿高德溫大收稅戶米，逮禦史獄。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Dewen, registrar of the imperial mausoleum district at Jiangling, greatly exacted rice from tax households and was seized by the censorial prison.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gao Dewen, registrar of the imperial mausoleum district at Jiangling, had extorted large amounts of rice from tax households and was arrested by the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 汝霖具二法上。

translations.literal: Rulin submitted two punishments upward.
translations.idiomatic: Rulin submitted two alternative penalties for the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 世宗責之曰：「朕以卿為公正，故登用之。

translations.literal: Shizong reproved him, saying, "I regarded you as impartial and therefore elevated and employed you.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong rebuked him: "I promoted you because I thought you impartial.

sentences.zh: 德溫有人在宮掖，故朕頗詳其事。

translations.literal: Dewen has someone in the inner palace; therefore I am quite familiar with this affair.
translations.idiomatic: Dewen has connections in the inner palace, so I know this case well.

sentences.zh: 朕肯以宮掖之私撓法耶？

translations.literal: Would I bend the law for private palace interests?
translations.idiomatic: Would I bend the law for palace favoritism?

sentences.zh: 不謂卿等顧徇如是。」

translations.literal: I did not expect that you and the others would show partiality to this degree."
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect you to show such partiality."

sentences.zh: 汝霖跪謝。

translations.literal: Rulin knelt in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Rulin knelt and apologized.

sentences.zh: 久之，上顧左諫議大夫楊伯仁曰：「台官不正如此。」

translations.literal: After a long while the emperor turned to Left Remonstrator Yang Boren and said, "The censorial officials are not upright to this extent."
translations.idiomatic: After a while the emperor turned to Left Remonstrator Yang Boren and said, "The censorial officials are this corrupt."

sentences.zh: 伯仁奏曰：「罪疑惟輕，故具二法上請，在陛下裁斷耳。

translations.literal: Boren memorialized, saying, "When guilt is doubtful, one should lean toward leniency; therefore two punishments were submitted for Your Majesty's decision.
translations.idiomatic: Boren replied, "When guilt is uncertain, the law favors leniency; that is why two penalties were submitted for Your Majesty to decide.

sentences.zh: 且人材難得，與其材智而邪，不若用愚而正者。」

translations.literal: Moreover, talent is hard to obtain; rather than use the clever but crooked, it is better to use the dull but upright."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, good men are hard to find; better a dull but upright official than a clever but corrupt one."

sentences.zh: 上作色曰：「卿輩皆愚而不正者也。」

translations.literal: The emperor changed color and said, "You people are all dull but not upright."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened. "You are all dull and not upright."

sentences.zh: 未幾，複坐失出大興推官高公美罪，謫授棣州防禦使。

translations.literal: Before long, again because he failed to expose the crime of Gao Gongmei, push-official of Daxing, he was demoted and appointed Defender of Di Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again demoted—for failing to expose the offenses of Gao Gongmei, push-official of Daxing—and appointed Defender of Di Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 頃之，複為太子少師兼禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 拜參知政事，太子少師如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Grand Councillor, his post as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Grand Councillor while retaining his post as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 是日，汝霖兄汝弼亦進拜尚書左丞，時人榮之。

translations.literal: That same day Rulin's elder brother Rubi was also advanced to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; people of the time regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Rulin's elder brother Zhang Rubi was also promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, to the envy of contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 後因朝奏日論事上前，世宗謂曰：「朕觀唐史，見太宗行事初甚厲精，晚年與群臣議多飾辭，朕不如是也。」

translations.literal: Later, on a day when court was held and he discussed affairs before the throne, Shizong said to him, "When I read Tang history, I see that in the beginning Taizong's conduct was very strenuous, but in his later years in deliberating with his ministers he often used ornamented language; I am not like that."
translations.idiomatic: Later, during a court session when he was discussing affairs before the throne, Shizong said to him, "Reading Tang history, I see that Taizong at first was fiercely diligent, but in his later years his discussions with ministers were often mere fine phrases; I am not like that."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「唐太宗，明天子也，晚年亦有過舉。

translations.literal: He also said, "Tang Taizong was an enlightened sovereign, yet in his later years he also had faults.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Emperor Taizong of Tang was an enlightened ruler, yet even he erred in his later years.

sentences.zh: 朕雖不能比跡聖帝明王，然常思始終如一。

translations.literal: Although I cannot match the footsteps of sage emperors and enlightened kings, I constantly think of being the same from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot match sage-kings and enlightened rulers, but I constantly strive to be the same man from first to last.

sentences.zh: 今雖年高，敬慎之心無時或怠。」

translations.literal: Now though I am advanced in years, the heart of reverent caution never slackens for a moment."
translations.idiomatic: Though I am old now, my reverent caution never slackens for a moment."

sentences.zh: 汝霖對曰：「古人有言，'靡不有初，鮮克有終'，有始有卒者，其惟聖人乎！

translations.literal: Rulin replied, "The ancients had a saying: 'There is hardly anything without a beginning, but few can keep the end'—to have a beginning and a conclusion, is it not only the sage!
translations.idiomatic: Rulin replied, "The ancients said, 'Everything has a beginning, but few keep the end'—only the sage has both beginning and end!

sentences.zh: 魏徵所言守成難者，正謂此也。」

translations.literal: What Wei Zheng meant in saying that preserving the achievement is hard refers precisely to this."
translations.idiomatic: What Wei Zheng meant when he said that preserving what has been won is hard refers precisely to this."

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought it correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，章宗以原王判大興府事，上命汝霖但涓視事日且加輔導。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Zhangzong, as Prince Yuan, was assigned to administer the affairs of Daxing Prefecture; the emperor ordered Rulin to attend only on days when there was business and to give him added guidance.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year Zhangzong, as Prince Yuan, was put in charge of Daxing Prefecture; the emperor ordered Rulin to attend only on days when there was business and to tutor him closely.

sentences.zh: 尋坐擅支東宮諸皇孫食料，奪官一階。

translations.literal: Before long, because he had disbursed on his own authority the food allowances of the Eastern Palace's imperial grandsons, he was stripped of one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was demoted one rank for disbursing on his own authority the food allowances of the Eastern Palace's imperial grandsons.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 是時，世宗在位久，熟悉天下事，思得賢材與圖致治，而大臣皆依違苟且，無所薦達。

translations.literal: At that time Shizong had long been on the throne and was thoroughly familiar with affairs under Heaven; he wished to obtain worthy talent with which to seek good government, but the great ministers all vacillated and were perfunctory, recommending no one.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shizong had reigned long and knew the realm thoroughly; he wanted worthy men with whom to pursue good government, but his chief ministers all hedged and muddled through, recommending no one.

sentences.zh: 一日，世宗召宰臣謂曰：「卿等職居輔相，曾無薦舉何也？

translations.literal: One day Shizong summoned the chief ministers and said, "You hold the rank of chief ministers—how is it that you have never made recommendations?
translations.idiomatic: One day Shizong summoned the chief ministers and said, "You sit in the highest offices—why have you never recommended anyone?

sentences.zh: 且卿等老矣，殊無可以自代者乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, you are old; is there truly no one among you who could replace yourselves?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, you are old; is there really no one among you fit to succeed you?

sentences.zh: 惟朕嘗言某人可用，然後從而言之。

translations.literal: Only when I have said that a certain man may be used do you then follow and speak of him.
translations.idiomatic: Only when I say that someone is usable do you chime in.

sentences.zh: 卿等既無所言，必待朕知而後進用，將複有幾？」

translations.literal: Since you have nothing to say, if appointment must wait until I know of a man before he is advanced, how many more will there be?"
translations.idiomatic: If you offer nothing yourselves and men are promoted only after I have discovered them, how many more years will that take?"

sentences.zh: 因顧汝霖曰：「若右丞者，亦因右丞相言而知也。」

translations.literal: He then turned to Rulin and said, "As for a vice director such as this one—he too became known to me only because the right chancellor spoke of him."
translations.idiomatic: He then turned to Rulin and said, "Take the vice director here—even he came to my attention only because the right chancellor mentioned him."

sentences.zh: 汝霖對曰：「臣等苟有所知，豈敢不薦，但無人耳。」

translations.literal: Rulin replied, "If we had any knowledge of men, how would we dare not recommend them? It is only that there are no men."
translations.idiomatic: Rulin replied, "Had we known anyone worthy, we would never have hesitated to recommend him. The trouble is simply that there is no one."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「春秋諸國分裂，土地偏小，皆稱有賢。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "In the Spring and Autumn period the states were divided and their lands were small, yet each claimed to have worthies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "In the Spring and Autumn era the states were fragmented and their territories small, yet each still claimed to possess worthy men.

sentences.zh: 今天下之大，豈無人才？

translations.literal: Today the realm is vast—how can there be no talent?
translations.idiomatic: Today the realm is vast—how can there be no talent?

sentences.zh: 但卿等不舉而已。

translations.literal: It is only that you do not recommend them, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: It is only that you refuse to recommend anyone.

sentences.zh: 今朕自勉，庶幾致治。

translations.literal: Now I shall exert myself, and perhaps we may attain good government.
translations.idiomatic: Now I must drive myself on if we are ever to reach good government.

sentences.zh: 他日子孫誰與共治乎？」

translations.literal: In days to come, with whom will my descendants govern together?"
translations.idiomatic: When I am gone, with whom will my descendants share the work of rule?"

sentences.zh: 汝霖等皆有慚色。

translations.literal: Rulin and the others all showed shame on their faces.
translations.idiomatic: Rulin and the others could only sit there, ashamed.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，進拜平章政事，兼修國史，封芮國公。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was advanced to Grand Councilor, concurrently compiler of the national history, and enfeoffed as Duke of Rui.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was promoted to Grand Councilor, made concurrent compiler of the national history, and enfeoffed as Duke of Rui.

sentences.zh: 世宗不豫，與太尉徒單克甯、右丞相襄同受顧命。

translations.literal: When Shizong fell ill, together with Grand Marshal Tushan Kening and Right Chancellor Xiang he received the imperial testament.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong fell ill, he and Grand Marshal Tushan Kening and Right Chancellor Xiang together received the dying emperor's testament.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位。

translations.literal: Zhangzong ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 加銀青榮祿大夫，進封莘。

translations.literal: He was given the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver-Green Tally and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He received the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver-Green Tally and was promoted to Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 先是，右丞相襄言：「熙宗聖節蓋七月七日，為系景宣忌辰，更用正月受外國賀。

translations.literal: Earlier, Right Chancellor Xiang had said, "Emperor Xizong's sacred birthday was originally the seventh day of the seventh month; because of Jingxuan's death anniversary it was changed, and the first month was used instead to receive foreign congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Right Chancellor Xiang had said, "Emperor Xizong's sacred birthday fell on the seventh day of the seventh month, but because of Jingxuan's death anniversary it was moved, and foreign congratulations were received in the first month instead.

sentences.zh: 今天壽節在七月，雨水淫暴，外方人使赴闕，有礙行李，乞移他月為便。」

translations.literal: Today the Heavenly Longevity Festival falls in the seventh month, when rain is torrential; envoys from distant regions coming to court are hindered in their baggage. I beg that it be moved to another month for convenience."
translations.idiomatic: Today the Heavenly Longevity Festival falls in the seventh month, when rains are violent; envoys from abroad traveling to court are impeded on the road. I ask that it be shifted to another month for their convenience."

sentences.zh: 汝霖言：「帝王之道當示信於天下。

translations.literal: Rulin said, "The way of emperors and kings should display trustworthiness to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Rulin said, "The way of kings is to show the realm that one's word can be trusted.

sentences.zh: 昔宋主構生日，亦系五月。

translations.literal: Formerly the Song emperor Gou's birthday also fell in the fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor Gou's birthday also fell in the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 是時，都在會甯，上國遣使賜禮，不聞有霖潦礙阻之說。

translations.literal: At that time both courts were at Huining; our state sent envoys to grant birthday gifts, and one never heard talk of heavy rain and flooding obstructing the journey.
translations.idiomatic: At that time both courts were at Huining, and our state sent envoys with birthday gifts across thousands of miles without anyone citing floods as an excuse for delay.

sentences.zh: 今與宋構好日久，遽以暑雨為辭，示以不實。

translations.literal: Now that we have long been on good terms with Song, to take sudden refuge in summer rain as an excuse would show insincerity.
translations.idiomatic: We have been at peace with Song for many years; to plead summer rains now would expose us as insincere.

sentences.zh: 萬一雨水逾常，愆期到闕，猶愈更用別日。」

translations.literal: Even if the rain should exceed the norm and their arrival at court be delayed past the appointed day, that is still better than changing to another day."
translations.idiomatic: Even if the rains are worse than usual and the envoys miss the appointed day, that is still preferable to changing the festival outright."

sentences.zh: 參知政事劉瑋、御史大夫唐括貢、中丞李晏、刑部尚書兼右諫議大夫完顏守貞、修起居注完顏烏者、同知登聞檢院事孫鐸亦皆言其不可。

translations.literal: Vice Grand Councilor Liu Wei, Censor-in-Chief Tangut Gong, Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Yan, Minister of Justice and concurrent Right Remonstrance Officer Wanyan Shouzhen, diarist Wanyan Wuzhe, and Associate Director of the Petition Office for Hearing Grievances Sun Duo also all said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councilor Liu Wei, Censor-in-Chief Tangut Gong, Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Yan, Minister of Justice and Right Remonstrance Officer Wanyan Shouzhen, diarist Wanyan Wuzhe, and Associate Director of the Petition Office Sun Duo likewise all opposed the change.

sentences.zh: 帝初從之，既而竟用襄議。

translations.literal: The emperor at first followed them, but in the end adopted Xiang's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at first sided with them, but in the end adopted Xiang's proposal.

sentences.zh: 時帝在諒陰，初出獵，諫院聯章言心喪中未宜。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was in the mourning hut; when he first went out hunting, the Remonstrance Bureau submitted a joint memorial saying that during heart mourning it was not yet appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then in mourning for Shizong; when he first went out hunting, the Remonstrance Bureau submitted a joint memorial arguing that hunting was improper while he was still in heart mourning.

sentences.zh: 其後冬獵，汝霖諫之。

translations.literal: Later, on the winter hunt, Rulin remonstrated against it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the winter hunt came round, Rulin remonstrated again.

sentences.zh: 詔答曰：「卿能每事如此，朕複何憂。

translations.literal: An edict replied, "If you can speak thus on every matter, what have I to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: An edict answered him, "If you will speak up on every matter like this, what have I to fear?

sentences.zh: 然時異事殊，難同古昔，如能斟酌得中，斯為當矣。」

translations.literal: Yet times differ and affairs change; it is hard to match antiquity. If one can weigh matters and hit the mean, that is what is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Yet times change and ancient precedent cannot be copied wholesale. What matters is to weigh each case and strike the right balance."

sentences.zh: 一日，帝謂宰臣曰：「今之用人，太拘資歷，如此何能得人？」

translations.literal: One day the emperor said to the chief ministers, "In appointing men today you are too bound by seniority—how can you obtain people that way?"
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor told his chief ministers, "You are too rigid about seniority in appointments—how can you ever find the right men that way?"

sentences.zh: 汝霖奏曰：「不拘資格，所以待非常之材。」

translations.literal: Rulin reported, "Not being bound by qualifications is how one treats extraordinary talent."
translations.idiomatic: Rulin replied, "Waiving formal qualifications is reserved for truly extraordinary talent."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「崔祐甫為相，未逾年薦八百人，豈皆非常材耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "When Cui Youfu was chancellor he recommended eight hundred men in less than a year—were they all extraordinary talent?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Cui Youfu as chancellor recommended eight hundred men in under a year—were they all extraordinary?"

sentences.zh: 時有司言民間收藏制文，恐因而滋訟，乞禁之。

translations.literal: At that time the responsible offices said that the people privately kept copies of statutes and feared that lawsuits would thereby multiply, and begged that it be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: About then the responsible offices reported that commoners were keeping private copies of statutes and that this might breed litigation, and asked that the practice be banned.

sentences.zh: 汝霖謂：「王者之法，譬猶江、河，欲使易避而難犯。

translations.literal: Rulin said, "The law of kings is like the Yangtze and Yellow rivers—one wishes to make transgression easy to avoid and hard to commit.
translations.idiomatic: Rulin said, "A king's law should be like the great rivers: easy to steer clear of and hard to violate.

sentences.zh: 本朝法制，坦然明白，今已著為不刊之典，天下之人無不聞誦。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's legal system is open and clear; it has now been set down as an immutable canon, and everyone under Heaven has heard and recited it.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's laws are plain and public; they are now fixed as permanent statutes, and everyone in the realm knows them by heart.

sentences.zh: 若令私家收之，則人皆曉然不敢為非，亦助治之一端也。

translations.literal: If private households are allowed to keep them, then all will understand clearly and not dare do wrong—this too is one means of aiding governance.
translations.idiomatic: If households may keep copies, people will know the law for themselves and hesitate to break it—that itself helps good government.

sentences.zh: 不禁為便。」

translations.literal: Not forbidding it is best."
translations.idiomatic: It is better not to forbid the practice."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued an edict adopting his view.

sentences.zh: 明昌元年三月，表乞致仕，不許。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Mingchang he memorialized begging to retire; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Mingchang 1 he submitted a memorial asking to retire; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 十二月，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he died.

sentences.zh: 時帝獵饒陽，訃聞，敕百官送葬，賻禮加厚，諡曰文襄。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was hunting at Raoyang; when word of his death arrived, he ordered all officials to attend the funeral, increased the condolence gifts, and gave the posthumous title Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then hunting at Raoyang; when news of his death arrived, he ordered the whole bureaucracy to attend the funeral, added to the condolence gifts, and granted the posthumous title Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 汝霖通敏習事，凡進言必揣上微意，及朋附多人為說，故言不忤而似忠也。

translations.literal: Rulin was quick and practiced in affairs; whenever he offered counsel he gauged the emperor's hidden intent, and with many partisans speaking for him, his words did not offend yet seemed loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Rulin was quick-witted and experienced in affairs; whenever he spoke he gauged the emperor's hidden intent, and with many allies speaking for him, his words never offended yet seemed loyal.

sentences.zh: 初，章宗新即位，有司言改造殿庭諸陳設物，日用繡工一千二百人，二年畢事。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhangzong had newly taken the throne, the responsible offices reported that the palace halls' furnishings were to be remade, requiring twelve hundred embroiderers each day and two years to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhangzong's reign the responsible offices proposed remaking the palace furnishings, requiring twelve hundred embroiderers a day and two years to finish.

sentences.zh: 帝以多費，意輟造。
