translations.literal: The emperor, considering the expense great, intended to halt the work.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, finding the cost excessive, intended to halt the project.

sentences.zh: 汝霖曰：「此非上服用，未為過侈。

translations.literal: Rulin said: "These are not items for the sovereign's personal use and are not excessively lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Rulin said, "These are not for the sovereign's personal use and are not excessively lavish.

sentences.zh: 將來外國朝會，殿宇壯觀，亦國體也。」

translations.literal: When foreign states come to court in future, stately halls are also a matter of national dignity."
translations.idiomatic: When foreign states come to court, stately halls are also a matter of national dignity."

sentences.zh: 其後奢用浸廣，蓋汝霖有以導之雲。

translations.literal: Afterward extravagant spending gradually spread—Rulin had surely helped guide it.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward extravagant spending gradually spread—Rulin had surely helped guide it.

sentences.zh: 張玄素，字子真，與浩同曾祖。

translations.literal: Zhang Xuansu, style name Zizhen, shared a great-grandfather with Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuansu, whose style name was Zizhen, shared a great-grandfather with Zhang Hao.

sentences.zh: 祖祐，父匡，仕遼至節度使。

translations.literal: His grandfather was You; his father Kuang—both served Liao and reached the rank of military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather You and his father Kuang had both served the Liao and risen to military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 玄素初以廕得官。

translations.literal: Xuansu at first received office by yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Xuansu first entered office through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 高永昌據遼陽，玄素在其中。

translations.literal: Gao Yongchang held Liaoyang; Xuansu was within the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yongchang seized Liaoyang, Xuansu was inside the city.

sentences.zh: 斡魯軍至，乃開門出降，特授世襲銅州猛安。

translations.literal: When Walu's army arrived, he opened the gates and came out to surrender; he was specially granted the hereditary meng'an of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Walu's army arrived, he opened the gates and surrendered; he was specially granted the hereditary meng'an post at Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天會間，曆西上閣門使、客省使、東宮計司。

translations.literal: During the Tianhui era he successively held the posts of Western Upper Gate Commissioner, Guest Reception Commissioner, and Eastern Palace Accounts Office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhui era he served in turn as Western Upper Gate Commissioner, Guest Reception Commissioner, and Eastern Palace Accounts Office.

sentences.zh: 天眷元年，以靜江軍節度使知涿州，察廉最，進官一階。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjuan he was made military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army with concurrent administration of Zhuo Prefecture; on integrity inspection he ranked highest and was advanced one rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjuan 1 he was appointed military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army and put in charge of Zhuo Prefecture; on the integrity review he ranked at the top and was promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 皇子魏王道濟遙領中京，以玄素為魏王府同提點，尋改鎮西軍節度使，遷東京路都轉運使，改興平軍節度使。

translations.literal: The imperial prince, Prince of Wei Daoji, held the Central Capital in absentia; Xuansu was made co-intendant of the Prince of Wei's mansion, then transferred to military commissioner of the Zhenxi Army, promoted to transport commissioner of the Eastern Capital Circuit, and then made military commissioner of the Xingping Army.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daoji of Wei held the Central Capital in absentia; Xuansu was made co-intendant of his household, then transferred to military commissioner of the Zhenxi Army, promoted to transport commissioner of the Eastern Capital Circuit, and finally made military commissioner of the Xingping Army.

sentences.zh: 正隆末年，天下盜起，玄素發民夫增築城郭，同僚諫止之，不聽。

translations.literal: In the late Zhenglong era bandits rose throughout the realm; Xuansu mobilized corvée labor to heighten the walls and moats, and his colleagues remonstrated and tried to stop him, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Zhenglong era bandits rose everywhere; Xuansu drafted laborers to raise the walls and moats. His colleagues urged him to stop, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，寇掠鄰郡，皆無備，而興平獨安。

translations.literal: Before long bandits raided neighboring commanderies, all of which were unprepared, while Xingping alone remained secure.
translations.idiomatic: Soon raiders struck neighboring prefectures, none of which was ready, while Xingping alone stayed safe.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，玄素來見於東京。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, Xuansu came to see him at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne, Xuansu came to pay his respects at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 玄素在東京，希海陵旨，言世宗嘗取在官黃糧，及摭其數事。

translations.literal: While at the Eastern Capital, to please Hailing's intent he had said that Shizong had once taken yellow grain from government stores, and had also gathered up several such matters.
translations.idiomatic: While still at the Eastern Capital he had curried favor with Hailing by reporting that Shizong had once taken government grain for his own use and by collecting several similar charges.

sentences.zh: 至是來見，世宗一切不問。

translations.literal: Now, on coming to audience, Shizong ignored every one of them.
translations.idiomatic: When he now came to audience, Shizong ignored every charge.

sentences.zh: 玄素與李石力言宜早幸燕京，上深然之。

translations.literal: Xuansu and Li Shi strongly urged that he should promptly visit Yanjing; the emperor deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: Xuansu and Li Shi strongly urged an early move to Yanjing, and the emperor was deeply convinced.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部尚書，出鎮定武，遂致仕。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Revenue, went out to command Dingwu, and then retired.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Revenue, took command at Dingwu, and then retired.

sentences.zh: 年八十四，卒。

translations.literal: At age eighty-four he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 玄素厚而剛毅，人畏憚之。

translations.literal: Xuansu was generous and stern; people feared and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuansu was generous in manner but stern in temper, and people feared as well as respected him.

sentences.zh: 往往以片紙署字其上治瘧疾，輒愈，人皆異之。

translations.literal: He would often write characters on a slip of paper to treat malaria, and it would invariably be cured; people all regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: He often wrote a few characters on a scrap of paper to treat malaria, and the illness invariably cleared—people marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 張汝弼

translations.literal: Zhang Rubi
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rubi

sentences.zh: 汝弼，字仲佐，父玄征，彰信軍節度使，玄素之兄也。

translations.literal: Rubi, style name Zhongzuo; his father was Xuanzheng, military commissioner of the Zhangxin Army and elder brother of Xuansu.
translations.idiomatic: Rubi, whose style name was Zhongzuo, was the son of Xuanzheng, military commissioner of the Zhangxin Army and elder brother of Xuansu.

sentences.zh: 汝弼初以父廕補官。

translations.literal: Rubi at first received office through his father's yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Rubi first entered office through his father's hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，中進士第，調沈州樂郊縣主簿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed registrar of Yuejiao County in Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 2 he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed registrar of Yuejiao County in Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 玄征妻高氏與世宗母貞懿皇后有屬，世宗納玄征女為次室，是為元妃。

translations.literal: Xuanzheng's wife, the Gao clan, was related to Shizong's mother Empress Zhenyi; Shizong took Xuanzheng's daughter as his second consort—she who became Consort Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzheng's wife, née Gao, was kin to Shizong's mother Empress Zhenyi; Shizong took Xuanzheng's daughter as his second consort, who became known as Consort Yuan.

sentences.zh: 張氏生趙王允中。

translations.literal: Of the Zhang clan she bore Prince Zhao Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Prince Zhao, Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位于遼陽，汝弼與叔玄素俱往歸之，擢應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne at Liaoyang, Rubi and his uncle Xuansu both went to join him, and Rubi was promoted to Hanlin Academy Attendant for Imperial Orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne at Liaoyang, Rubi and his uncle Xuansu both went to join him; Rubi was promoted to Hanlin Academy Attendant for Imperial Orders.

sentences.zh: 世宗禦翠巒閣，召左司郎中高衎及汝弼問曰：「近日除授，外議何如？

translations.literal: Shizong held court at the Cuiluan Pavilion and summoned Left Department Director Gao Yan and Rubi, asking, "On recent appointments, what is the talk outside?
translations.idiomatic: Shizong held audience at the Cuiluan Pavilion and summoned Left Department Director Gao Yan and Rubi, asking, "What is being said outside about the recent appointments?

sentences.zh: 宜以實奏，毋少隱也。

translations.literal: You should report truthfully and not conceal anything.
translations.idiomatic: Report the truth and hold nothing back.

sentences.zh: 有不可用者當改之。」

translations.literal: If any are unfit they should be changed."
translations.idiomatic: If anyone is unfit, he should be replaced."

sentences.zh: 衎、汝弼皆無以對。

translations.literal: Gao and Rubi both had nothing to say.
translations.idiomatic: Gao and Rubi had nothing to say.

sentences.zh: 自皇統以來，內藏諸物費用無度，吏夤緣為奸，多亡失。

translations.literal: From Huangtong onward the inner storehouses' goods were spent without limit; clerks used connections to commit fraud, and much was lost.
translations.idiomatic: From Huangtong on spending from the inner storehouses knew no limit; clerks traded on connections to cheat the court, and vast quantities vanished.

sentences.zh: 汝弼與宮籍直長高公穆、入殿小底王添兒閱實之，以類為籍，作四庫以貯之。

translations.literal: Rubi, together with the director of palace registers Gao Gongmu and inner-hall attendant Wang Tian'er, audited the goods, classified them by category into registers, and made four storehouses to hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Rubi, with Director of Palace Registers Gao Gongmu and inner-hall attendant Wang Tian'er, audited the stores, drew up categorized registers, and organized four warehouses to hold them.

sentences.zh: 於是，內藏庫使王可道等皆杖一百，汝弼等各進階。

translations.literal: Thereupon the inner-storehouse commissioner Wang Kedao and others were each beaten one hundred strokes, and Rubi and the others were each advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: The inner-storehouse commissioner Wang Kedao and others were each flogged one hundred strokes, while Rubi and his colleagues were each promoted.

sentences.zh: 頃之，兼修起居注，轉右司員外郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was made concurrent diarist and transferred to Outer-office Director of the Right Department.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made concurrent diarist and transferred to Outer-office Director of the Right Department.

sentences.zh: 母憂去官。

translations.literal: He left office on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 起複吏部郎中，累遷吏部尚書，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning as Outer-office Director of the Ministry of Personnel, he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Personnel and appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning as Outer-office Director of the Ministry of Personnel, he rose in stages to Minister of Personnel and was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 詔徙女直猛安謀克於中都，給以近郊官地，皆鹆脊薄。

translations.literal: An edict moved Jurchen meng'an and mouke to the Central Capital and granted them official land in the near suburbs—all of it barren, rocky, and thin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict relocated Jurchen meng'an and mouke households to the Central Capital and allotted them official fields in the near suburbs—all of it stony, thin soil.

sentences.zh: 其腴田皆豪民久佃，遂專為己有。

translations.literal: The fertile fields had long been rented by powerful families and were thus held as their own.
translations.idiomatic: The rich land had long been leased by powerful families, who treated it as private property.

sentences.zh: 上出獵，猛安謀克人前訴所給地不可種藝，詔拘官田在民久佃者與之。

translations.literal: The emperor went out hunting; meng'an and mouke leaders came before him to complain that the land given them could not be planted; an edict ordered that official fields long rented by commoners be seized and given to them.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was out hunting, meng'an and mouke leaders came forward to say the allotted land could not be farmed; he ordered official fields that commoners had long rented to be taken back and given to them.

sentences.zh: 因命汝弼議其事。

translations.literal: He then ordered Rubi to deliberate on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Rubi to work out a policy.

sentences.zh: 請「條約立限，令百姓自陳。

translations.literal: He requested, "Draw up regulations and set a time limit, allowing the people to report on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Rubi proposed, "Lay down clear rules and a deadline, and let commoners come forward on their own.

sentences.zh: 過限，許人首告，實者與賞。」

translations.literal: After the limit, allow others to lodge accusations; if the report proves true, grant a reward."
translations.idiomatic: After the deadline, let others inform against offenders; if the charge is proved, give the informer a reward."

sentences.zh: 上可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 仍遣同知中都轉運使張九思拘籍之。

translations.literal: He still sent Associate Transport Commissioner of the Central Capital Zhang Jiusi to seize and register the fields.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Associate Transport Commissioner of the Central Capital Zhang Jiusi to seize and register the fields.

sentences.zh: 上問：「高麗、夏皆稱臣。

translations.literal: The emperor asked, "Goryeo and Xia both call themselves vassals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Goryeo and Western Xia both style themselves our vassals.

sentences.zh: 使者至高麗，與王抗禮。

translations.literal: When envoys reach Goryeo they exchange equal ritual with the king.
translations.idiomatic: When our envoys reach Goryeo they stand as equals with the king.

sentences.zh: 夏王立受，使者拜，何也？」

translations.literal: The Xia king stands to receive them while the envoys bow—why is that?"
translations.idiomatic: The Xia king stands to receive them while our envoys bow—why the difference?"

sentences.zh: 左丞襄對曰：「故遼與夏為甥舅，夏王以公主故，受使者拜。

translations.literal: Left Vice Grand Councilor Xiang replied, "Formerly Liao and Xia were nephew and uncle by marriage; the Xia king, because of the princess, received envoys' bows while standing.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Grand Councilor Xiang answered, "Under the Liao, Xia was a nephew state by marriage; because of the Liao princess, the Xia king stood to receive our envoys' bows.

sentences.zh: 本朝與夏約和，用遼故禮，所以然耳。」

translations.literal: Our dynasty made peace with Xia under the old Liao ritual, and that is why it is so."
translations.idiomatic: Our court made peace with Xia on Liao terms, and that is why the practice continues."

sentences.zh: 汝弼曰：「誓書稱一遵遼國舊儀，今行之已四十年，不可改也。」

translations.literal: Rubi said, "The oath document states that we follow the Liao state's former ritual in full; it has now been practiced for forty years and cannot be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Rubi said, "The treaty oath says we follow Liao ritual in full; that usage has stood for forty years and should not be altered."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿等言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What you say is right."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 上聞尚書省除授小官多不稱職，召汝弼至香閣謂之曰：「他宰相年老，卿等宜盡心。」

translations.literal: Hearing that many minor appointments from the Department of State Affairs were unfit for their posts, he summoned Rubi to the Fragrant Pavilion and told him, "The other chief ministers are old; you should give your utmost effort."
translations.idiomatic: Learning that many junior appointments from the Department of State Affairs were incompetent, he summoned Rubi to the Fragrant Pavilion and said, "Your fellow chief ministers are old; you must shoulder the work."

sentences.zh: 汝弼對曰：「材薄不足以副聖意耳。」

translations.literal: Rubi replied, "My talent is thin and insufficient to match the sage's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Rubi replied, "My ability is too slight to live up to Your Majesty's expectations."

sentences.zh: 進拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 於是，戶部糶官倉粟，汝弼請使暖湯院得糴之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Revenue Ministry was selling grain from the official granaries; Rubi requested that the Nuantang Courtyard be allowed to purchase it.
translations.idiomatic: About then the Revenue Ministry was selling grain from the state granaries; Rubi asked that the Nuantang Courtyard be allowed to buy it.

sentences.zh: 上讓曰：「汝欲積陰德邪？

translations.literal: The emperor reproved him, saying, "Do you wish to accumulate hidden merit?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reproved him: "Are you trying to bank secret merit?

sentences.zh: 何區區如此。」

translations.literal: Why be so petty about this?"
translations.idiomatic: Why fuss over something so small?"

sentences.zh: 左丞相徒單克甯得解政務，為樞密使。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Tushan Kening was relieved of government duties and made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Tushan Kening was released from civil administration and made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 是日，汝弼亦懷錶乞致仕。

translations.literal: That same day Rubi also submitted a memorial in his breast begging to retire.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Rubi too submitted a retirement petition from his sleeve.

sentences.zh: 上使人止之曰：「卿年未老，未可退也。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent someone to stop him, saying, "You are not yet old and may not withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent word to refuse him: "You are not yet old; you may not retire."

sentences.zh: 進左丞，與族弟參知政事汝霖同日拜，族裏以為榮。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Left Vice Director and, on the same day as his clansman the Vice Grand Councilor Rulin, received appointment; the clan regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director and, on the same day as his kinsman Vice Grand Councilor Rulin, took office—a glory for the whole clan.

sentences.zh: 有年未六十而乞致仕者，上不許。

translations.literal: When someone not yet sixty begged to retire, the emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: If a man under sixty asked to retire, the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 汝弼曰：「聖旨嘗許六十致仕。」

translations.literal: Rubi said, "The imperial instruction once permitted retirement at sixty."
translations.idiomatic: Rubi said, "Your Majesty's instruction once allowed retirement at sixty."

sentences.zh: 上責之曰：「朕嘗許至六十者致仕，不許未六十者。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him, saying, "I once promised that those who reach sixty may retire from office, and I do not permit those who have not yet reached sixty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him: "I promised retirement only to those who reach sixty—not to anyone younger.

sentences.zh: 且朕言六十致仕，是則可行，否則當言。

translations.literal: Moreover, when I spoke of retiring at sixty, if that could be done, it should be done; if not, you should have said so.
translations.idiomatic: When I set retirement at sixty, that was a policy you could accept or challenge—you should have spoken up then.

sentences.zh: 卿等不言，皆此類也。」

translations.literal: You all said nothing—everything is of this kind."
translations.idiomatic: You all kept silent. This is exactly the sort of thing I mean."

sentences.zh: 久之，坐擅增諸皇孫食料，與丞相守道、右丞粘割斡特剌、參政張汝霖各削官一階。

translations.literal: After some time, for having on his own authority increased the food allowances of the imperial grandsons, together with the Chief Councillor Shoudao, the Right Councillor Niagua Wetela, and the Participating Councillor Zhang Rulin, each had one rank in office reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for unilaterally increasing the imperial grandsons' provisions, he and Chief Councillor Shoudao, Right Councillor Niagua Wetela, and Participating Councillor Zhang Rulin were each demoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「准法當解職，但示薄責耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "According to the law he ought to be removed from office, but this is only a light reprimand."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The law would require dismissal; I am only imposing a mild penalty."

sentences.zh: 汝弼在病告，上謂宰相曰：「汝弼久居執政，練習制度，頗能斟酌人材，而用心不正。」

translations.literal: While Rubi was on sick leave, the emperor told the chief ministers, "Rubi has long held power in the government, is practiced in the institutions, and is quite able to weigh men's talents, yet his intentions are not upright."
translations.idiomatic: While Rubi was on medical leave, the emperor told the chief ministers, "Rubi has long been in power, knows the institutions well, and can judge talent—but his heart is not straight."

sentences.zh: 乃罷為廣甯尹，賜通犀帶。

translations.literal: He was then dismissed and made Guangning Yin, and was granted a rhinoceros-horn belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office and appointed Guangning Yin, and given a rhinoceros-horn belt.

sentences.zh: 汝弼為相，不能正諫。

translations.literal: As chief minister, Rubi could not remonstrate uprightly.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister, Rubi never offered direct, principled remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 上所欲為，則順而導之，所不欲為，則微言以觀其意。

translations.literal: What the emperor wished to do, he would comply with and guide; what the emperor did not wish to do, he would hint at obliquely to gauge his intent.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor wanted something done, Rubi would smooth the way; when the emperor did not, he would drop a hint to test his mood.

sentences.zh: 上責之，則婉辭以引過，終不忤之也。

translations.literal: When the emperor reproached him, he would use gentle words to draw blame upon himself, and in the end never opposed him.
translations.idiomatic: When rebuked, he would speak softly and take the blame, and never in the end defied the throne.

sentences.zh: 而上亦知之。

translations.literal: The emperor knew this as well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew this too.

sentences.zh: 且黷貨，以計取諸家名園甲第珍玩奇好，士論薄之。

translations.literal: Moreover he was greedy for goods, and by calculation seized from various families famous gardens, fine mansions, and rare curios and choice objects; public opinion held him in low esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He was also corrupt, scheming to seize famous gardens, grand houses, and rare treasures from one family after another, and men of judgment despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he died.

sentences.zh: 汝弼既與永中，甥舅，陰相為黨。

translations.literal: Rubi was related to Yongzhong as maternal uncle and nephew, and in secret they formed a faction together.
translations.idiomatic: Rubi and Yongzhong were uncle and nephew by marriage, and they secretly acted as a faction.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，汝弼妻高氏每以邪言怵永中，覬非望，畫永中母像，侍奉祈祝，使術者推算永中。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong took the throne, Rubi's wife, the Gao clan, often used perverse words to stir Yongzhong, coveting an improper destiny; she had a portrait painted of Yongzhong's mother, attended it with offerings and prayers, and had diviners cast Yongzhong's horoscope.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhangzong's accession, Rubi's wife Lady Gao repeatedly whispered sedition to Yongzhong, nursing ambitions beyond his station: she had Yongzhong's mother painted for worship and prayer, and employed diviners to read Yongzhong's fate.

sentences.zh: 有司鞫治，高氏伏誅。

translations.literal: The authorities investigated and tried the case; Lady Gao was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the authorities investigated, Lady Gao was put to death.

sentences.zh: 事連汝弼，上以事覺在汝弼死後，得免削奪。

translations.literal: The affair implicated Rubi, but because the crime came to light only after Rubi's death, he was spared posthumous stripping of honors.
translations.idiomatic: The case touched Rubi, but because it came to light only after his death, his honors were not posthumously revoked.

sentences.zh: 耶律安禮

translations.literal: Yelu Anli
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Anli

sentences.zh: 耶律安禮，本名納合，系出遙輦氏。

translations.literal: Yelu Anli, original name Nahe, was descended from the Yaolian clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Anli, whose original name was Nahe, came from the Yaolian line.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned in childhood, he was known for serving his mother with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he became known for filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 遼季，間關避難，未嘗一日怠溫凊。

translations.literal: In the late Liao, amid hardship and flight he never for a single day neglected the warmth and coolness due a parent.
translations.idiomatic: In the chaos at the end of Liao, through every hardship of exile, he never for a day failed in the daily care owed a parent.

sentences.zh: 入朝，當路者重其行義，使主帥府文字，授左班殿直。

translations.literal: After entering our court, those in power valued his conduct and righteousness and had him handle documents in the Marshal's Office; he was appointed Left Guard Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After he entered Jin service, men in power respected his character and made him handle documents in the Marshal's Office; he was appointed Left Guard Attendant.

sentences.zh: 天眷初，從元帥于山西。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianjuan era he followed the Marshal into Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianjuan era he followed the Marshal into Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 母喪，不克歸葬，主帥憐之，賻禮甚厚。

translations.literal: When his mother died he could not return home to bury her; the Marshal pitied him and gave him very generous funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he could not go home to bury her; the Marshal took pity on him and gave lavish funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 安禮冒大暑，挽柩行千餘裏，哀毀骨立，行路嗟歎。

translations.literal: Anli braved the great heat, drew the bier more than a thousand li, and in grief wasted away until only bone remained; travelers on the road sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Anli endured the fierce summer heat and drew the bier more than a thousand li; grief wore him to skin and bone, and wayfarers marveled aloud.

sentences.zh: 服除，由行台吏、禮部主事累遷工部侍郎，改左司郎中。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he rose from clerk of the Branch Secretariat through Supervisor of the Ministry of Works to Left Department Director.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he rose from clerk of the Branch Secretariat and supervisor in the Ministry of Works to Director of the Left Department.

sentences.zh: 天德間，罷行台尚書省，入為工部侍郎，累遷本部尚書。

translations.literal: During the Tiande period, when the Branch Secretariat was abolished, he entered the capital as Vice Minister of Works and was promoted in succession to Minister of that ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiande period, when the Branch Secretariat was abolished, he entered court as Vice Minister of Works and eventually became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，為宋國歲元使。

translations.literal: The next winter he served as envoy for the Song state's New Year tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he served as envoy for the Song New Year mission.

sentences.zh: 被詔鞫治韓王亨獄于廣寧。

translations.literal: He was ordered to investigate the case of Prince Han Wang Heng at Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to try the case of Prince Han, Wang Heng, at Guangning.

sentences.zh: 亨無反狀，安禮還奏。

translations.literal: Heng showed no sign of rebellion; Anli returned and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Heng showed no sign of rebellion; Anli returned and so reported.

sentences.zh: 海陵怒，疑安禮梁王宗弼故吏，乃責安禮曰：「孛迭有三罪。

translations.literal: Hailing was angry and suspected that Anli, as a former subordinate of Prince Liang Zongbi, rebuked Anli, saying, "Li Dielie is guilty of three crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was furious, suspecting that Anli—as a former man of Prince Liang Zongbi—was shielding Heng. He rebuked Anli: "Li Dielie is guilty of three crimes.

sentences.zh: 其論阿裏出虎有誓券不當死，既引伏。

translations.literal: His argument that Alihutuhu had a sworn bond and ought not die—he has already confessed to that.
translations.idiomatic: His claim that Alihutuhu had a sworn bond and should not die—he has already confessed to that.

sentences.zh: 其謂不足進馬，及密遣刺客二者，安得無之？

translations.literal: As for his saying that horses were not worth presenting, and secretly sending assassins—how can these not exist?
translations.idiomatic: As for saying the horses were unworthy to present, and secretly dispatching assassins—can those be denied?

sentences.zh: 汝等來奏，欲測我喜怒以為輕重耳。」

translations.literal: You come to report in order to test my pleasure and anger and treat the matter as light or heavy—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: You report to me only to gauge my mood and decide how hard to press—that is all this is."

sentences.zh: 乃遣安禮再往，與李老僧同鞫之。

translations.literal: He then sent Anli back, together with Li Laoseng, to investigate again.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Anli back with Li Laoseng to investigate again.

sentences.zh: 老僧由是殺亨於獄。

translations.literal: Laoseng thereby killed Heng in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Laoseng thereupon killed Heng in prison.

sentences.zh: 海陵猶謂安禮輒殺亨以絕滅事蹟，親戚得以不坐。

translations.literal: Hailing still believed that Anli had on his own killed Heng to cut off the trail of the affair, so that kinsmen could escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing still believed Anli had killed Heng on his own initiative to destroy the evidence and spare the clan.

sentences.zh: 安禮之不附上刻下乃如此。

translations.literal: Anli's refusal to fawn on superiors and strike at subordinates was like this.
translations.idiomatic: This was how Anli refused to flatter those above and crush those below.

sentences.zh: 改吏部尚書，護大房山諸陵工作。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel and supervised the work on the imperial tombs at Mount Dafang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of personnel and supervised work on the imperial tombs at Mount Dafang.

sentences.zh: 拜樞密副使，封譚國公，遷尚書右丞，進封郕國公，轉左丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Tan, transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Cheng, and then transferred to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Tan, promoted to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, advanced to Duke of Cheng, and then made left vice director.

sentences.zh: 議降累朝功臣封爵，密諫伐江南，忤海陵意，罷為南京留守，封溫國公。

translations.literal: He debated reducing the enfeoffments of meritorious ministers of successive reigns, secretly remonstrated against campaigning in Jiangnan, offended Hailing's intent, was dismissed as Military Governor of the Southern Capital, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He argued for reducing the enfeoffments of meritorious ministers of past reigns, secretly remonstrated against the Jiangnan campaign, offended Hailing, was dismissed to serve as military governor of the Southern Capital, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wen.

sentences.zh: 安禮長於吏事，廉謹自將，從帥府再伐宋，寶貨人口一無所取。

translations.literal: Anli was skilled in administrative affairs and restrained himself with integrity and caution; following the marshalate on a second campaign against Song, he took neither goods nor persons.
translations.idiomatic: Anli excelled in administrative affairs and conducted himself with integrity; on a second Song campaign with the marshalate he took neither goods nor captives.

sentences.zh: 貴為執政，奴婢止數人，皆有契券，時議賢之。

translations.literal: Though he rose to chief minister, he kept only a few slave servants, all with written contracts, and public opinion praised his worth.
translations.idiomatic: Though he rose to chief minister, he kept only a few household servants, all with written contracts, and contemporaries praised his worth.

sentences.zh: 薨，年五十六。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died, aged fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 納合椿年，本名烏野。

translations.literal: Na Hechunnian, original name Wuye.
translations.idiomatic: Na Hechunnian, whose original name was Wuye.

sentences.zh: 初置女直字，立學官於西京，椿年與諸部兒童俱入學，最號警悟。

translations.literal: When the Jurchen script was first established, a school was set up in the Western Capital; Chunnian entered school with children of the various tribes and was foremost in quickness of understanding.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchen script was first created and a school opened in the Western Capital, Chunnian studied with children of the tribes and was the quickest to learn.

sentences.zh: 久之，選諸學生送京師，俾上京教授耶魯教之，椿年在選中。

translations.literal: After some time, selected students were sent to the capital to be taught by Yelu of the Upper Capital; Chunnian was among those chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Later, outstanding students were sent to the capital for instruction by a Yelu teacher from the Upper Capital; Chunnian was among them.

sentences.zh: 補尚書省令史，累官殿中侍御史，改監察禦史。

translations.literal: He was appointed clerk of the Imperial Secretariat and rose in succession to Attendant Censor in the Palace, then was changed to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He became a clerk of the Imperial Secretariat, rose to Palace Attendant Censor, and was then made Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 海陵為相，薦為右司員外郎，編定新制。

translations.literal: When Hailing was Chief Councillor, he recommended him as Outer Director of the Right Department to compile and fix the new regulations.
translations.idiomatic: While Hailing was Chief Councillor, he recommended Chunnian as Outer Director of the Right Department to draft the new code.

sentences.zh: 海陵篡立，以為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Hailing usurped the throne, he made him Remonstrating Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing seized the throne, he appointed him Remonstrating Grandee.

sentences.zh: 椿年有酒失，海陵使之戒酒，遂終身不復飲。

translations.literal: Chunnian had a fault involving wine; Hailing ordered him to give up drink, and from then on he never drank again for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Chunnian had a drinking problem; Hailing ordered him to abstain, and he never touched wine again for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 改秘書監，修起居注，授世襲猛安，為翰林學士兼禦史中丞。

translations.literal: He was changed to Director of the Secretariat, compiled the Veritable Records, was granted a hereditary military command, and became Hanlin Academician concurrently with Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He became Director of the Secretariat, compiled the Veritable Records, received a hereditary military command, and served as Hanlin Academician and Censor-in-Chief at once.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，起上京諸猛安於中都、山東等路安置，以勞賜玉帶閑廄馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era, when the military households of the Upper Capital were resettled in the Central Capital, Shandong, and other circuits, he was rewarded for his labor with a jade belt and horses from the imperial stud.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhenyuan, when Upper Capital military households were resettled in the Central Capital, Shandong, and other circuits, he was rewarded for the labor with a jade belt and stud horses.

sentences.zh: 奉遷山陵，還為都點檢。

translations.literal: He attended the transfer of the imperial tombs, and on his return became Chief Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the removal of the imperial tombs and, on returning, became Chief Commandant.

sentences.zh: 賜今名，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: He was granted his present name and appointed Participating Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He was given his present name and appointed Participating Councillor.

sentences.zh: 海陵謂椿年曰：「如卿吏材甚難得，複有如卿者乎？」

translations.literal: Hailing said to Chunnian, "Men of your administrative talent are very hard to obtain—is there another like you?"
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said to Chunnian, "Officials of your caliber are rare—is there another like you?"

sentences.zh: 椿年薦大理丞紇石烈婁室。

translations.literal: Chunnian recommended the Grand Court Judge Hesilie Loushi.
translations.idiomatic: Chunnian recommended Grand Court Judge Hesilie Loushi.

sentences.zh: 海陵以婁室為右司員外郎。

translations.literal: Hailing made Loushi Outer Director of the Right Department.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing appointed Loushi Outer Director of the Right Department.

sentences.zh: 未旬日，海陵謂椿年曰：「吾試用婁室，果如卿言。

translations.literal: Within ten days Hailing said to Chunnian, "I tried Loushi, and it is truly as you said.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Hailing told Chunnian, "I tried Loushi, and he is exactly as you said.

sentences.zh: 惟賢知賢，信矣。」

translations.literal: Only the worthy know the worthy—how true that is."
translations.idiomatic: Only the worthy recognize the worthy—how true that is."

sentences.zh: 婁室後賜名良弼，有宰相才，世宗時，至左丞相，號賢相焉。

translations.literal: Loushi was later granted the name Liangbi; he had the talent of a chief minister, and in Shizong's time rose to Left Chief Councillor and was called a worthy minister.
translations.idiomatic: Loushi was later given the name Liangbi. He had chief-ministerial talent; under Shizong he rose to Left Chief Councillor and was hailed as a worthy minister.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，椿年薨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong, Chunnian died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenglong, Chunnian died.

sentences.zh: 海陵親臨哭之，追封特進、譚國公，諡忠辯，賻銀二千兩、彩百端、絹千匹、錢千萬。

translations.literal: Hailing came in person to mourn him, posthumously enfeoffed him as Special Advancement-holder and Duke of the State of Tan, gave him the posthumous title Zhongbian, and granted funeral gifts of two thousand taels of silver, a hundred rolls of brocade, a thousand bolts of silk, and ten million cash.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing came in person to mourn him, posthumously enfeoffed him Special Advancement-holder and Duke of Tan, gave the posthumous name Zhongbian, and granted two thousand taels of silver, a hundred rolls of brocade, a thousand bolts of silk, and ten million cash for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 以長子參謀合為定遠大將軍，襲猛安，次子合答為忠武校尉。

translations.literal: His eldest son Canmou He was made General of the Pacification of the Far, inheriting the military command; his second son Heda was made Loyal Martial Regiment Commander.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Canmou He was made General of the Pacification of the Far and inherited the command; his second son Heda was made Loyal Martial Regiment Commander.

sentences.zh: 及歸葬，再賜錢百萬，仍給道路費。

translations.literal: When the burial procession returned home, he was again granted a million cash and travel expenses on the road were provided.
translations.idiomatic: When the body was returned for burial, another million cash was granted and road expenses were supplied.

sentences.zh: 椿年有宰相才，好推挽士類，然頗營產業，為子孫慮。

translations.literal: Chunnian had the talent of a chief minister and liked to lift up men of the scholar class, yet he rather built up property and made plans for his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Chunnian had chief-ministerial talent and liked to advance scholars, yet he also amassed property for his descendants.

sentences.zh: 冒占西南路官田八百餘頃。

translations.literal: He falsely occupied more than eight hundred qing of official land on the Southwest Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He seized more than eight hundred qing of official land on the Southwest Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大定中，括撿田土，百姓陳言官豪佔據官地，貧民不得耕種。

translations.literal: In the Dading period, when land was surveyed and registered, common people petitioned that powerful families had seized official land and the poor could not farm.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dading period, during a land survey, commoners petitioned that the powerful had seized official fields and the poor could not plant.

sentences.zh: 溫都思忠子長壽、椿年子猛安參謀合等三十余家凡冒占三千餘頃。

translations.literal: Wendusi Zhong's son Changshou, Chunnian's son the military commander Canmou He, and more than thirty other households altogether falsely occupied more than three thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: Wendusi Zhong's son Changshou, Chunnian's son Canmou He, and more than thirty other households had seized over three thousand qing in all.

sentences.zh: 詔諸家除牛頭稅地各再給十頃，其餘盡賦貧民種佃。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that each household, apart from ox-head tax land, be given another ten qing, and that the remainder all be assigned to poor people to plant and rent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ruled that each household keep its ox-head tax land plus ten more qing, and that the rest be given to the poor to farm on rent.

sentences.zh: 世頗以此譏椿年雲。

translations.literal: The age rather used this to ridicule Chunnian.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries often cited this to mock Chunnian.

sentences.zh: 祁宰，字彥輔，江淮人。

translations.literal: Qi Zai, style name Yanfu, was a man of the Jianghuai region.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Zai, courtesy name Yanfu, was from the Jianghuai region.

sentences.zh: 宋季以醫術補官。

translations.literal: In the late Song he entered office through medical skill.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Song he entered office through medicine.

sentences.zh: 王師破汴得之，後隸太醫。

translations.literal: When the royal army took Bian he was captured, and afterward was attached to the Imperial Medical Service.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin army took Bian he was captured and later assigned to the Imperial Medical Service.

sentences.zh: 累遷中奉大夫、太醫使。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Grand Master of Palace Attendance and Imperial Medical Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Grand Master of Palace Attendance and Imperial Medical Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 數被賞賚，常感激欲自效。

translations.literal: Repeatedly rewarded, he was often moved with gratitude and wished to repay the favor.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly rewarded by the throne, he burned to repay the favor.

sentences.zh: 海陵將伐宋，宰欲諫，不得見。

translations.literal: When Hailing was about to attack Song, Zai wished to remonstrate but could not obtain an audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing prepared to attack Song, Zai wished to remonstrate but could not gain an audience.

sentences.zh: 會元妃有疾，召宰診視。

translations.literal: It happened that the primary consort fell ill, and Zai was summoned to examine her.
translations.idiomatic: Then the primary consort fell ill and Zai was summoned to treat her.

sentences.zh: 既入見，即上疏諫，其略言：「國朝之初，祖宗以有道伐無道，曾不十年，蕩遼戡宋。

translations.literal: Once he had entered and been seen, he at once submitted a remonstrance; in summary it said: "At the beginning of our dynasty, the ancestors, using the Way to attack those without the Way, in less than ten years overthrew Liao and defeated Song.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he was admitted to audience, he submitted a memorial of remonstrance. In essence it read: "At the founding of our dynasty, the ancestors took the realm by right against wrong; in less than ten years they overthrew Liao and crushed Song.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，上有武元、文烈英武之君，下有宗翰、宗雄謀勇之臣，然猶不能混一區宇，舉江淮、巴蜀之地，以遺宋人。

translations.literal: At that time, above there were the martial and civil founders, heroic rulers, and below there were Zonghan and Zongxiong, ministers of counsel and valor—yet still they could not unify the realm, and they left the lands of the Jianghuai and Bashu to the Song people.
translations.idiomatic: Even then, though above stood the martial Wuyuan and civil Wenlie, heroic founders, and below stood Zonghan and Zongxiong, bold in counsel and battle, they still could not unite the realm and left Jianghuai and Bashu to Song.

sentences.zh: 況今謀臣猛將，異于曩時。

translations.literal: How much more are today's strategists and fierce generals unlike those of old.
translations.idiomatic: How much less can today's strategists and generals match those men.

sentences.zh: 且宋人無罪，師出無名。

translations.literal: Moreover the Song people are without guilt; to march out is without a righteous name.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Song has committed no crime; to march against them is to march without just cause.

sentences.zh: 加以大起徭役，營中都，建南京，繕治甲兵，調發軍旅，賦役煩重，民人怨嗟，此人事之不修也。

translations.literal: Added to this are the great levies of corvée labor, the building of the Central Capital, the establishment of the Southern Capital, the repair of armor and weapons, the mobilization of armies—the levies and services are heavy and the people groan in resentment: this is the failure to govern human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On top of that come massive corvée levies: building the Central Capital, establishing the Southern Capital, repairing arms, mobilizing armies—taxes and labor crush the people and resentment fills the land. This is failure in human affairs.

sentences.zh: 間者晝星見於牛鬥，熒惑伏於翼軫。

translations.literal: Recently a comet appeared in the Ox and Dipper, and Mars lay hidden in the Wings and Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Recently a comet appeared in the Ox and Dipper, and Mars lay hidden in the Wings and Chariot.

sentences.zh: 巳歲自刑，害氣在揚州，太白未出，進兵者敗，此天時不順也。

translations.literal: The year ji is self-punishing; harmful qi lies in Yangzhou; Venus has not yet risen—those who advance troops will be defeated: this is Heaven's seasons out of accord.
translations.idiomatic: The ji year brings self-punishment; malignant qi gathers at Yangzhou; Venus has not yet risen—armies that advance will be defeated. This is Heaven out of season.

sentences.zh: 舟師水涸，舳艫不繼，而江湖島渚之間，騎士馳射，不可驅逐，此地利不便也。」

translations.literal: The river fleets are stranded as the waters fail, and the ships cannot follow; yet among the rivers, lakes, and islets, Song horsemen gallop and shoot and cannot be driven off—this is the terrain unfavorable to us."
translations.idiomatic: River fleets are stranded as the waters fall and ships cannot keep pace; yet among rivers, lakes, and islets Song horsemen ride and shoot and cannot be driven away. This is terrain against us."

sentences.zh: 言甚激切。

translations.literal: His words were very forceful.
translations.idiomatic: His words were fierce and unsparing.

sentences.zh: 海陵怒，命戮於市，籍其家產，天下哀之。

translations.literal: Hailing was enraged and ordered him executed in the market; his household property was confiscated, and all under Heaven mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was enraged and ordered him executed in the marketplace; his property was confiscated, and the realm mourned him.

sentences.zh: 綦戩，宰婿也，海陵疑奏疏戩為之。

translations.literal: Qi Zhan, Zai's son-in-law, was suspected by Hailing of having written the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Zhan, Zai's son-in-law, was suspected by Hailing of having drafted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「實不知也。」

translations.literal: He pleaded, saying, "I truly did not know."
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded, "I truly knew nothing of it."

sentences.zh: 海陵猶杖戩。

translations.literal: Hailing still had Zhan beaten with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing had Zhan beaten with the staff anyway.

sentences.zh: 召禁中諸司局官至鹹德門，諭以殺宰事。

translations.literal: He summoned officials of the various bureaus in the Inner Palace to the Xiande Gate and announced the killing of Zai.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned bureau officials of the Inner Palace to Xiande Gate and announced Zai's execution.

sentences.zh: 明年，世宗即位於遼東。

translations.literal: The next year Shizong took the throne in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Shizong took the throne in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔贈資政大夫，複其田宅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict posthumously granted him Grand Master of Governance and restored his fields and house.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year an edict posthumously made him Grand Master of Governance and restored his fields and house.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，詔訪其子忠勇校尉、平定州酒監公史，擢尚藥局都監。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong took the throne, an edict sought out his son, the Loyal and Valiant Regiment Commander and wine inspector of Pingding Prefecture, Gongshi, and promoted him to Director of the Imperial Pharmacy Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong took the throne, an edict sought out his son Gongshi, Loyal and Valiant Regiment Commander and wine inspector of Pingding, and promoted him to Director of the Imperial Pharmacy Bureau.

sentences.zh: 泰和初，詔定功臣諡，尚書省掾李秉鈞上言：「事有宜緩而急，若輕而重者，名教是也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, an edict fixed posthumous titles for meritorious ministers; Li Bingjun, a clerk of the Imperial Secretariat, submitted a statement: "There are matters that ought to be treated as urgent yet are delayed, and as light yet are heavy—such is the teaching of names and principles.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe, when posthumous titles for meritorious ministers were fixed, Secretariat clerk Li Bingjun submitted: "Some matters should be urgent yet are delayed, light yet weighed heavy—such is the force of moral principle.

sentences.zh: 伏見故贈資政大夫祁宰以忠言被誅，慕義之士，盡傷厥心。

translations.literal: I observe that the late Grand Master of Governance Qi Zai was put to death for loyal words; men who admire righteousness were all wounded in heart.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that the late Grand Master of Governance Qi Zai was executed for loyal counsel; every man who honors righteousness was wounded to the heart.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，贈之以官，陛下錄用其子，甚大惠也。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne he was posthumously granted office; Your Majesty employed his son—a very great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne he was posthumously honored; Your Majesty employed his son—a great grace.

sentences.zh: 雖武王比干之墓，孔子譽夷、齊之仁，何以異此。

translations.literal: Though King Wu repaired Bi Gan's tomb and Confucius praised the benevolence of Bo Yi and Shu Qi, how does this differ from that?
translations.idiomatic: King Wu restored Bi Gan's tomb; Confucius praised Bo Yi and Shu Qi—how is this any different?

sentences.zh: 而有司拘文，以職非三品不在議諡之例，臣竊疑之。

translations.literal: Yet the offices cling to the letter of the law, saying that because his post was not of the third rank he falls outside the rule for debating a posthumous title—I venture to doubt this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the offices cling to the letter of the law, holding that because his rank was not third grade he falls outside the rule for posthumous titles—I find that doubtful.

sentences.zh: 若職至三品方得請諡，當時居高官、食厚祿者，不為無人，皆畏罪淟涊，曾不敢申一喙，畫一策，以為社稷計。

translations.literal: If only when one's post reaches the third rank may one request a posthumous title, then at that time among those who held high office and ate rich stipends there were not none—yet all feared guilt and were filthy with flattery; not one dared open his mouth or draw up a single plan for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: If posthumous titles require third-rank office, then in that day men of high rank and rich stipends were not lacking—yet all feared punishment and smeared themselves with flattery; not one dared speak or offer a single plan for the realm.

sentences.zh: 卒使立名死節之士，顧出於醫卜之流，亦可以少愧矣。

translations.literal: In the end it took a man who established his name by dying for principle to stand forth from the class of physicians and diviners—this too may shame them a little.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the man who won fame by dying for principle came from the ranks of physicians—enough, perhaps, to shame them a little.

sentences.zh: 臣以謂非常之人，當以非常之禮待之。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that an extraordinary man should be treated with extraordinary rites.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that an extraordinary man deserves extraordinary honor.

sentences.zh: 乞詔有司特賜諡以旌其忠，斯亦助名教之一端也。」

translations.literal: I beg that an edict order the offices specially to grant a posthumous title to commend his loyalty—this too would be one means of upholding the teaching of names."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty order the offices to grant a special posthumous title to honor his loyalty—this too would uphold moral principle."

sentences.zh: 制曰：「可。」

translations.literal: The rescript said: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The rescript read: "Approved."

sentences.zh: 下太常，諡曰忠毅。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and the posthumous title Loyal and Resolute was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: The order went to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, which granted the posthumous title Loyal and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：異哉，海陵之為君也，舞智禦下而不恤焉。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Strange indeed was Hailing as ruler—he displayed cleverness to control his subordinates yet showed them no care.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: How strange a ruler Hailing was—clever in managing those below him, yet indifferent to their welfare.

sentences.zh: 君子仕于朝，動必以禮，然後免於恥。

translations.literal: When a gentleman serves at court, every act must accord with ritual—only then can he escape disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: When a gentleman serves at court, every act must follow ritual—only then can he avoid disgrace.

sentences.zh: 張通古、耶律安禮位不及張浩，進退始終，其賢遠矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Tonggu and Yelu Anli did not rank as high as Zhang Hao, but in advance and retreat they held to principle throughout—their worth was far greater.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tonggu and Yelu Anli never rose as high as Zhang Hao, yet in how they advanced and withdrew they held to principle throughout—their worth was far greater.

sentences.zh: 浩無事不為，無役不從，為相最久，用之厚，遇之薄，豈亦自取之邪？

translations.literal: Hao had no affair in which he did not take part, no labor from which he held back; he served as chief minister longest, was used generously yet treated stingily—was this not also something he brought on himself?
translations.idiomatic: Hao took part in every affair and every task; he served as chief minister longer than any other, was used to the full yet rewarded thinly—was that not partly of his own choosing?

sentences.zh: 海陵伐宋，浩、安禮位皆大臣，一以婉辭，一以密諫，賢於不諫而已。

translations.literal: When Hailing campaigned against Song, Hao and Anli both held high ministerial rank—one remonstrated in indirect language, one in secret memorial—better only than not remonstrating at all.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing campaigned against Song, Hao and Anli were both great ministers—one remonstrated in guarded language, one in a secret memorial—no more than better than silence.

sentences.zh: 祁宰一醫流，獨能極諫，其後皆如所言。

translations.literal: Qi Zai was but a physician by trade, yet he alone could remonstrate to the utmost; afterward everything happened as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Zai was only a physician by profession, yet he alone remonstrated to the full; afterward everything unfolded as he had warned.

sentences.zh: 海陵戕之，足以成其百世之名耳。

translations.literal: Hailing killed him—enough to secure his name for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing put him to death—and in doing so secured his fame for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 納合椿年援引善類，有君子風。

translations.literal: Na Hechunnian drew up men of talent and had the bearing of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Na Hechunnian promoted men of talent and carried himself with the bearing of a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 其死適在宋兵未舉之前，然觀其好營產殖，亦未必忘身徇國之士也。

translations.literal: His death happened just before the Song armies marched, yet judging from his delight in amassing property, he was hardly a man who forgot himself for the state.
translations.idiomatic: He died just before the Song armies marched, yet given his zeal for amassing property, he was hardly a man who would forget himself for the realm.

sentences.zh: 祁宰卓乎不可及也夫！

translations.literal: Qi Zai stands eminent—beyond reach!
translations.idiomatic: As for Qi Zai—he stands alone, beyond comparison!
